Message:
fix(supabase): close the ACL rule gaps Codex and Copilot found (#2584)

Review fixes to the explicit table ACL rule:
- ignore GRANT/REVOKE text inside single-quoted literals (E'' escapes
  included) and nested block comments; dollar-quoted bodies stay SQL so
  dynamic DDL in a DO block still counts
- recognise quoted names ("public"."x") and CREATE UNLOGGED TABLE, and
  every table named in a multi-table drop statement
- keep an existing table's ACL through a no-op CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS
- bind each legacy exemption to its creating migration, so a legacy table
  that is removed and recreated without an ACL fails

Renegotiated pins (scorer-lock unlocks approved by Matthew on 2026-10-28):
scripts/lib/supabaseTableAclRules.mjs and
src/test/supabase-table-explicit-acl.test.ts. The check is stricter: the
new cases fail 13 ways against the previous rule.

Message:
fix(quick-log): cap a single watering at 50,000 ml with a clear message (#2110)

# Verdant Pull Request

> Production: https://verdantgrowdiary.com

## Summary

Production QA 2026-10-14: 1,000,000 ml saved without warning and became
the tent's last watering; 99,999,999 was blocked, but only as "must be a
positive number". The ceiling is now 50,000 ml (owner decision
2026-10-14), shared by the watering form builder, the inline save gate,
the review view model and the V2 save payload, with one message:
"Applied volume is too large (max 50,000 ml). Check the number and save
again."

Pins that encoded the old 1,000,000 bound are moved to the new ceiling
in the same commit. Feed volume and runoff bounds are unchanged.

## Files changed

- `src/lib/quickLogWateringFormViewModel.ts` —
`QUICK_LOG_WATER_VOLUME_MAX_ML`,
`QUICK_LOG_WATER_VOLUME_TOO_LARGE_MESSAGE`, new `volume_ml:too_large`
reason.
- `src/lib/quickLogWaterSaveGateRules.ts` — inline gate surfaces the
reason.
- `src/lib/quickLogWateringReviewViewModel.ts` — review preview stays in
needs-input above the ceiling.
- `src/lib/quickLogV2SavePayload.ts` — `volume_too_large` reason.
- `src/lib/quickLogSaveErrorMessage.ts` — operator message and recovery
copy for `volume_too_large`.
- `src/test/quick-log-water-volume-max.test.ts` — new.
- `src/test/quick-log-water-save-gate-rules.test.ts`,
`src/test/quick-log-watering-form-view-model.test.ts`,
`src/test/quick-log-watering-review-view-model.test.ts` — renegotiated
pins (old 1,000,000 bound).
- `src/lib/legacyQuickLogUnifiedSave.ts`, `src/components/QuickLog.tsx`,
`src/lib/publicQuickLogStarterRules.ts` — the public-starter legacy path
and starter validation use the same ceiling; legacy volume parsing and
starter validation reuse the Water form grammar via
`assessWateringVolumeInput` (raw starter text is checked before it is
stored).
- `src/lib/quickLogPendingWateringStore.ts` (`validRecord`) and
`src/lib/writeQuickLogWateringTypedEvent.ts`
(`mapWateringInputToRpcArgs`) — recovery-journal and writer validation
enforce `QUICK_LOG_WATER_VOLUME_MAX_ML`, so a pre-ceiling or crafted
retry journal cannot replay 50,001–1,000,000 ml.
- `src/lib/quickLogPendingStarterWaterStore.ts` (`validRecord`) — the
public-starter recovery journal replayed by `retryStarterWater` enforces
the ceiling on every read, claim and write.
- `src/test/quick-log-starter-water-recovery-volume-max.test.ts` — new
(50,000 claimable; 50,001 / 1,000,000 refused; a stored pre-ceiling
record reads as blocked).
- `src/lib/quickLogWaterVolumeWarningRules.ts` (from #2145, merged in) —
`LARGE_WATER_AMOUNT_HARD_MAX_ML` is now the 50,000 ml ceiling and
`QUICK_LOG_WATER_VOLUME_MAX_ML` derives from it; `assessWaterVolumeText`
returns a distinct `too_large` status. The form builder, review view
model, `assessWateringVolumeInput` and the 10,000 ml confirm warning
(now 10,000–50,000 ml) all use this one parser.
- `src/lib/quickLogPreviewRules.ts` — the legacy editor’s live preview
uses the same grammar and ceiling.
- `src/lib/wateringVolumeDefaultsViewModel.ts` — a historical watering
above the ceiling is skipped as a prefill default.
- `src/test/quick-log-starter-water-volume-max.test.tsx` — new (resumed
starter draft edited to 1,000,000 ml is refused before any save).
- `src/test/quick-log-pending-watering-store.test.ts`,
`src/test/write-quick-log-watering-typed-event.test.ts` — renegotiated
pins (see below).
- `src/lib/quickLogPendingStarterWaterStore.ts`
(`clearUnreadablePendingStarterWater`),
`src/lib/quickLogPendingWateringStore.ts`
(`clearUnreadablePendingQuickLogWatering`),
`src/lib/quickLogUnreadableWaterRecoveryRules.ts` (new),
`src/constants/quickLogWaterRecoveryCopy.ts` (new),
`src/components/QuickLog.tsx`, `src/components/QuickLogV2Sheet.tsx` —
"Check Timeline, then clear" escape for a recovery record that reads as
blocked (for example a pre-ceiling 1,000,000 ml record). Under the owner
recovery lock it removes only the owner-scoped unreadable key, never
replays the record, and leaves readable records, the other journal and
other owners’ keys alone (CodeRabbit 4315741282, Matthew 2026-10-19).
- `src/test/quick-log-unreadable-water-recovery-clear.test.ts`,
`src/test/quick-log-starter-unreadable-water-recovery.test.tsx`,
`src/test/quick-log-v2-unreadable-watering-recovery.test.tsx` — new.

## Renegotiated checks (scorer lock)

Approved by Matthew on 2026-10-18 (unlock declared with `node
scripts/scorer-lock.mjs --unlock`, reason: move the accepted-volume pins
from 1,000,000 ml to the owner-decided 50,000 ml ceiling, #2110 Codex

50,000 |

| 1,000,000 → `volume_ml:invalid` |

No other assertion in either file changed.

Second unlock, approved by Matthew on 2026-10-19 ("50,000 ml wins" over
#2145’s 1,000,000 ml hard max). Above-ceiling inputs now report the
distinct `volume_ml:too_large` reason, so the affected reason pins move
with the value:

| File | Check | Old | New |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/test/quick-log-water-volume-save-parser-parity.test.ts` |
"rejects a decimal just above the hard maximum that Number() rounds
down" | `1000000.00000000001` → `volume_ml:invalid` |

1,000,000 ok | 50,001 → `volume_ml:too_large`; 50,000 ok |
| `src/test/quick-log-water-volume-warning-boundaries.test.ts` | "does

| `src/test/quick-log-water-volume-warning-boundaries.test.ts` | "still
warns at the hard ceiling when it remains above 10,000 ml" | 1,000,000 |
50,000 |

No other assertion in those three files changed. All unlocks are
re-locked. The three earlier renegotiated files
(`quick-log-water-save-gate-rules`,
`quick-log-watering-form-view-model`,
`quick-log-watering-review-view-model`) are listed under Files changed;
they were not part of this unlock. The database-side ceiling remains out
of scope (no migration).

Third unlock, approved by Matthew on 2026-10-19 for these eight locked
files: `quick-log-pending-watering-store`,
`write-quick-log-watering-typed-event`,
`quick-log-water-save-gate-rules`,
`quick-log-water-volume-save-parser-parity`,
`quick-log-water-volume-warning-boundaries`,
`quick-log-water-volume-warning`, `quick-log-watering-form-view-model`,

commit:

| File | Check | Old | New |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src/test/quick-log-water-save-gate-rules.test.ts` | "blocks a
negative or huge volume" (Copilot 4305672182) | `toMatch(/too large (max
50,000 ml)/)` | `toBe(QUICK_LOG_WATER_VOLUME_TOO_LARGE_MESSAGE)` |
| `src/test/quick-log-watering-review-view-model.test.ts` | case title
only (Copilot 4305672202) | "…for mapper-invalid volume %j" | "…for
invalid or above-ceiling volume %j" |

`node scripts/scorer-lock.mjs --report --strict --base
origin/verdant-grow-diary` lists exactly these eight files as changed
and locked (exit 2 by design: every one is named in this body).

## Behavior changed

A watering above 50,000 ml is refused inline and on save with the
too-large message instead of being accepted or reported as "not a
positive number". A stored recovery record that can no longer be read
now shows a "Check Timeline, then clear" action instead of blocking
Water for the whole tab session; clearing sends nothing.

fix(quick-log): negative EC, fake png, Photo only (#2159 #2162 #2174) (#2196) Fixes #2159, #2162, and #2174. Head: `b11c17a4e867548026182905e6de94f3da6f405a` (was `02f5c96222aab4cb84e569cae6acf661e4aa5268` when this body was first written; see the repair section below). #2003 stays out of this PR. #2083 owned it and has since merged into `verdant-grow-diary` (`ec233259e`). ## Summary EC -1 says "EC can't be negative." A `.png` claim is accepted only when its bytes start with the PNG signature, including a file shorter than 8 bytes. "Photo only" writes a diary row with event type `photo`. `gallery.png` stays `image/jpeg`, which is what `makeImage("gallery.png")` produced on base. Only the fixture bytes changed. If the sheet unmounts after a Photo only upload succeeds, the insert still runs. Since `c3db89609`, the recovery lock for the exact scope and preallocated id is reserved before the upload starts and promoted before the insert is awaited (see the latest repair section). It stays while the insert is pending or ambiguous, and is released only on confirmed success or a definitive non-commit. A remount or reopen of the same plant cannot upload a second object or insert a second id. Reopening Plant Quick Log now reconciles that saved lock. When the exact owner-scoped diary row is readable, the session lock clears and Save is available again. A pending PNG check in the all-activities Photo editor is cancelled when the grower cancels or the target or selected draft resets, so the old file cannot land on the next plant. ## Tests run Unmount-during-save, fail-first: **2 failed, 0 passed**. After the fix: **those 2 passed**. Codex FAIL at `b4373f8f`, fail-first: photo-lock reconcile **1 failed**; pending PNG draft reset **2 failed**. After the fix: **3 passed**. Photo suites `plant-quick-log-photo-retry-recovery.test.tsx` and `plant-quick-log-photo-source-picker.integration.test.tsx`: **41 passed, 0 failed**. Related Photo only, short-PNG, recovery, funnel, and all-activities files, together with the new tests: **15 files, 170 passed, 0 failed**. `bun run typecheck` (`tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`): exit 0. ## Unlock receipt Cheeko via Verdante, 10:29 AM CT Oct 16, 2026: #2196: I approve unlocking only the fixture byte lines in locked plant-quick-log-photo-retry-recovery.test.tsx and plant-quick-log-photo-source-picker.integration.test.tsx (gallery.png case), replacing the 3-byte fake .png with a minimal valid PNG signature, no assertion changes, as their unlock receipt; writer bc-bcd09e18, fail-first, normal review path. ## Security checklist - [x] No client-trusted `user_id` (server always re-derives ownership via `auth.uid()`) - [x] No `service_role` introduced in frontend or Edge Functions - [x] RLS preserved on every touched table - [x] No fake live / demo data introduced or surfaced as real - [x] No new device-command / external-control surface introduced - [x] AI Coach unchanged - [x] Action Queue unchanged - [x] Tests added when behavior changes ## RLS / ownership impact None. The recovery fence is session storage only. The reopen check reads the signed-in owner's diary row by the stored id and clears the lock only when that id matches. ## AI Coach impact None. ## Action Queue impact None. ## Sensor / live-data truthfulness Negative EC is labeled as not a usable reading. ## External-control / device-command impact None. ## Repair after Codex P1 + CI FAIL at dd2e0ece3 (2026-10-16, Claude close-out session) Head moved `dd2e0ece30671fb1fa78ed29a150e79ed13e6e64` → `ca86b0f8e4d0c54afc77ed95ec5588ae21c907f0` by normal pushes only. - `b286a938a` merges `origin/verdant-grow-diary` at `bfd2a85c4`, which includes #2117 ("save a note with a photo as one diary row"). There were no textual conflicts. #2117 changes the note-with-photo path in `QuickLogV2Sheet.tsx`. This PR changes that file's PNG checks and the Plant Quick Log Photo only path, so the two do not overlap. #2117's own suite `quick-log-photo-note-single-row` passes on the merged tree. - `ca86b0f8e` fixes the Codex P1 at `PlantQuickLog.tsx:572` ("Retain confirmed photo saves after unmount"). The Photo only branch is now `persistPhotoOnlyEntry`, which works from the scope captured when Save was pressed. After a confirmed insert, telemetry, the recent target, `applyQuickLogV2Refresh` and the single `verdant:entry-created` dispatch run for that plant even if the sheet unmounted or switched plants. Only the sheet's own UI completion waits on `canContinue()`. Nothing fires before the insert is confirmed. - **Required shards 8/32 and 27/32 (FAIL at `dd2e0ece3`) were caused by this PR.** The Photo only branch sat above the main `quicklog_save_manual` path, so the first `rememberRecentQuickLogTarget(` and the first `"verdant:entry-created"` in the file came before `if (!result.ok)`. That ordering is pinned by `quick-log-recent-target-chip-wiring.test.ts` and `tired-grower-recovery-loop-journey.test.ts`. Both shards are green on deploy tip `bfd2a85c4`. Moving the helper below `handleSave` puts the order back, and both pins pass **unchanged**. Older findings, re-checked at the new head: - P1 `PlantQuickLog.tsx:544` (persist ambiguous identity across closure): **already fixed** at `b4373f8fa`/`dd2e0ece3`. Ambiguous and thrown inserts record the session-backed `quickLogPhotoAttachmentRecovery` lock with the exact preallocated id before the `canContinue()` check. Save also refuses while that lock exists. Proven by `issue-2174-photo-only-unmount-lock` (2 cases) and `issue-2174-photo-only-recovery-lock` (close and reopen: no second upload or insert). - P1 `PlantQuickLog.tsx:196` (reconcile the persisted lock on reopen): **already fixed** at `02f5c9622`. The open effect does the owner-scoped exact-id read and clears the lock once the row is readable. Proven by `issue-2174-photo-lock-reconcile`. - P1 `QuickLogAllActivitiesSection.tsx:1920` (invalidate pending PNG checks): **already fixed** at `02f5c9622`. Every `setPhotoFile(null)` reset path bumps `photoContentGenerationRef`: draft open, activity switch, target change, cancel and remove. Proven by `issue-2162-pending-png-draft-reset` (cancel and plant change). - CodeRabbit minor on `issue-2174-photo-only-retry-and-telemetry.test.tsx:129`: the telemetry assertion now sits inside `waitFor`. This is the only existing test edited, and it is this PR's own file. Tests - New `src/test/issue-2174-photo-only-confirmed-after-unmount.test.tsx` (3 cases). RED on the merged head: **2 failed / 1 passed** (unmount, target switch). GREEN: **3 passed**. - This PR's issue tests, #2117's single-row suite and the two pin files: **15 files, 56 passed, 0 failed**. - Every test file that references `PlantQuickLog`: **41 files, 507 passed, 1 failed**. The failure was a 5 s timeout in `plant-detail-one-tent-loop-quick-log-handoff` under parallel load. Re-run alone it gave **10/10 passed**. - Quick Log photo/PNG/media/exact-recovery/pending-note files: **11 files, 213 passed**. - Remaining files that reference `QuickLogV2Sheet` or `QuickLogAllActivitiesSection`: **67 files, 786 passed**. - `npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`: 0 diagnostics. `eslint` on changed files: 0 errors, plus 1 warning that is already on base (`useMemo` deps at `PlantQuickLog.tsx:275`). `prettier --check`: clean. `git diff --check`: clean. Overlap with draft #2200 (not touched): #2200 has the same blobs as this PR for `issue-2162-fake-png-content`, `issue-2174-photo-only-entry` and `issue-2159-negative-ec-message`, so the fake PNG content test **is** in #2196. Four test files exist only in #2200: `issue-2159-negative-ec-runoff-out.test.ts`, `quick-log-photo-content-rules.test.ts`, `ten-second-quick-check-photo-only.test.ts` and `search-shortcut-rules.test.ts`. Probed against this tree, the first three pass and the last fails, because `searchShortcutLabel` does not exist in the #2003 code that landed through #2083. #2200's `quickLogPhotoContentRules.ts` is an older 57-line version of this PR's rule. Claude repaired this PR and cannot give it a PASS. Exact-head re-review is requested from Blue Dream or Codex at `ca86b0f8e4d0c54afc77ed95ec5588ae21c907f0`. ## Repair after Codex FAIL at ca86b0f8e (2026-10-16, Claude close-out session) Head moved `ca86b0f8e4d0c54afc77ed95ec5588ae21c907f0` → `27aeff639775741c1649ba2c971c5f3a2a98e2c8` by one normal push (no rebase, no force). Base is still `verdant-grow-diary` at `bfd2a85c4`, so no merge was needed. **Codex P1, "Claim the pending Photo-only attempt before awaiting its insert" (`PlantQuickLog.tsx:704–716`): fixed in `27aeff639`.** At `ca86b0f8e` the lock was written only after `createQuickLogPhotoDiaryEntry` returned ambiguous. While the first insert was pending, an unmount and remount of the same plant found no lock, so a second Save uploaded again and inserted a second id. - `quickLogPhotoAttachmentRecovery.ts` has two new helpers. `claimQuickLogPhotoAttachmentRecoveryLock(scope, entryId)` writes the exact owner/grow/tent/plant scope and id to session storage and never replaces a different id. It returns `claimed`, `held_by_other` or `unavailable` (storage could not persist the claim). `releaseQuickLogPhotoAttachmentRecoveryLockForEntry(scope, entryId)` clears the lock only while it still holds that exact id. - `persistPhotoOnlyEntry` claims the scope and id **before** awaiting the insert.   on verdantgrowdiary.com."

  production). getPaddleEnvironment follows the resolved checkout: "live" on
  live checkout, else "sandbox". useMyEntitlements already reads live rows
  always; usePaddleCancelNotice would otherwise pick the sandbox row for a
  live subscriber, and sandbox test subscriptions stop unlocking once live.
- usePaddleCheckout: blocked only when the environment is "unavailable".
- checkoutTrustCopyRules: a "live" state with factual Paddle copy.
- .env.production carries the live client token (public by design).
  Correction to the handoff: the prebuild gate requires the bundled token to
  equal the committed .env.production, and restore-env-production-from-head
  resets that file to HEAD, so a build-env-only token would fail the build.
  The token ships in the same commit as the code that accepts it.
- .env.example documents the host rule.

GREEN after. Four locked tests rewritten to the new rule under Matthew's

Add consent-gated Ahrefs analytics, improve analytics consent handling, and refactor Grow Help Toolkit readiness and references (#1851)

### Motivation

- Add a second consent-gated analytics provider (Ahrefs Web Analytics)
alongside Google Analytics and make consent handling safer and more
explicit.
- Make shared Grow Help Toolkit planning inputs round-trip as
intentionally cleared (`null`) and centralize readiness checks so
calculations only run when required inputs are present.
- Surface source/method metadata and related resource backlinks in the
toolkit About panel and tighten copy about local-only behavior and
analytics provenance.

### Description

- Introduces Ahrefs analytics support via
`src/lib/ahrefsAnalyticsLoader.ts` and constants in
`src/constants/analytics.ts`, and wires it into a new runtime
coordinator `src/lib/analyticsConsentRuntime.ts` which applies the
consent decision for all providers and may request a reload when
necessary.
- Enhances the consent storage logic in `src/lib/analyticsConsent.ts` to
tolerate blocked `localStorage` with an in-memory fallback and to
publish cross-tab events; updates the banner and settings copy to
reference Ahrefs.
- Adds `src/lib/growHelpToolkitReadiness.ts` with `calculateWhenReady`
and several readiness predicates, updates multiple toolkit components
(`LightCalculatorTab`, `ExpenseCalculatorTab`, `NutrientCalculatorTab`,
export helpers, and state types) to use the readiness helpers and allow
certain shared fields to be `null` rather than auto-filled.
- Extracts the toolkit reference catalog to
`src/constants/growHelpToolkitReferences.ts` and updates the About panel
to render method notes and related internal resource backlinks; numerous
UI copy tweaks and small safety/formatting changes across pages.
- Adds comprehensive unit tests for analytics consent and loaders,
toolkit readiness, state persistence, exports, and UI behaviors under
`src/test/*` and updates existing static safety tests to include the new
analytics loader and runtime.

### Testing

- Ran the Vitest unit test suite including `analytics-consent.test.ts`,
`ahrefs-analytics-loader.test.ts`, `analytics-consent-runtime.test.ts`,
and the Grow Help Toolkit tests under `src/test/*`, and all tests
passed.
- Exercised integration points by running the static safety and
tag-presence checks (`google-analytics-static-safety.test.ts`,
`google-analytics-tag-presence.test.ts`), which confirmed consent gating
and absence of sensitive references.
- Exercised component-level behavior via DOM tests
(`grow-help-toolkit-page.test.tsx`, `grow-help-number-field.test.tsx`,
`public-vpd-calculator-page.test.tsx`), validating persisted `null`
round-trips, cleared-field behavior, and cross-tool links.
- Verified export and readiness logic with
`grow-help-toolkit-export.test.ts` and
`grow-help-toolkit-readiness.test.ts`, confirming calculations are
deferred until required inputs exist.

# Verdant Pull Request

> Production: https://verdantgrowdiary.com
> Please complete every section. Link to
[`docs/security-checklist.md`](../docs/security-checklist.md)
> and [`docs/security-exceptions.md`](../docs/security-exceptions.md)
when an
> item needs more context.

## Summary

Move AI Doctor (`ai-doctor-review`) and AI Coach (`ai-coach`) off the
Lovable AI gateway onto the Google Gemini API directly, through one
server-side helper. The two models stay the same. `GEMINI_API_KEY` is
read with `Deno.env` on the server only. A missing key fails closed with
today's user-facing behavior, before any credit spend. This PR does not
deploy Edge Functions. This PR does not remove or change any secret.

### Approval record

Matthew Cheek approved this slice directly in Canopy's chat on
2026-10-10 at 7:17 PM CT:

> Yes, build the Gemini-direct AI Doctor/Coach slice as a draft exactly
as Nursery scoped it.

Nursery relayed his 7:15 PM CT words:

> Build it with Google Gemini API direct, same models as today.

That yes is the owner-fence authorization for this slice only. Edge
Functions and the AI Doctor model stay on the owner-fence list for every
other change.

Matthew Cheek corrected the key-removal step directly in Canopy's chat
on 2026-10-10 at 8:04 PM CT: `LOVABLE_API_KEY` stays until every
remaining consumer and every rollback dependency has been separately
migrated and verified. Doctor/Coach success alone is not enough. This
body follows that correction.

Cheeko approved this PR at 2:08 PM CT on Oct 12, 2026. That approval is
not approval to create or set `GEMINI_API_KEY`, and it is not approval
to deploy. Those stay separate. `LOVABLE_API_KEY` still stays, per the
8:04 PM CT correction. The repo pause was lifted at 2:52 PM CT.

### Scope

- One helper, `supabase/functions/_shared/geminiDirectChat.ts`, resolves
provider and model per feature and tier and posts to Gemini's
OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- `supabase/functions/ai-doctor-review/index.ts` and
`supabase/functions/ai-coach/index.ts` call that helper.
- New Deno tests for route resolution, the missing-key fail-closed path,
and the request shape (mocked `fetch`, no live Gemini call).
- The existing hermetic AI Doctor Deno step in
`.github/workflows/ci.yml` now runs that new test beside
`providerUsageWiring.test.ts` and `stageTargetGrading.test.ts`. No prior
path was removed.
- Four coach source pins retargeted from the Lovable URL to
`fetch(GATEWAY_URL`, with the single-call, replay-before-fetch,
empty-short-circuit, and refund fences kept. Scorer lock was unlocked
for those four files and for `ci.yml` on this branch (habit H4). Doctor
safety and contract tests were not edited.

### Exclusions

- No schema change, no migration, no `supabase functions deploy`, no
secret create, set, read, or removal.
- No model escalation. `MODEL_TIER` stays `standard`.
- No client changes. `aiDoctorReviewResultContract.ts` checks, credit
charge and refund, receipts, `p_model_id` recording, and output tone and
structure stay as they are.
- `_shared/cost.ts` is a re-export of measurement helpers, not a
provider/model price table. It is unchanged. No Gemini price rows were
added.
- Other `LOVABLE_API_KEY` consumers are not migrated. The key stays. See
the dependency inventory and the corrected steps below.
- The generated `_shared/lib` mirror and `.sync-manifest.json` were not
edited. The helper does not import `src/lib`, so
`scripts/sync-edge-shared.mjs` was not run.
- This PR's source does not depend on removing `LOVABLE_API_KEY`.
`ai-doctor-review/index.ts` and `ai-coach/index.ts` at this head contain
neither `LOVABLE_API_KEY` nor `ai.gateway.lovable.dev`.

## Files changed

- `supabase/functions/_shared/geminiDirectChat.ts` — new provider/model
helper
- `supabase/functions/_shared/geminiDirectChat.test.ts` — new Deno tests
- `supabase/functions/_shared/geminiInlineImage.ts` — downloads a signed
storage object and builds a bounded Gemini data URL
- `supabase/functions/ai-doctor-review/index.ts` — doctor calls the
helper; HMAC frame is prompt contract v2; Gemini 429 is a quota failure
- `supabase/functions/ai-coach/index.ts` — coach calls the helper;
signed photos are inlined; Gemini 429 is a quota failure
- `src/test/gemini-direct-review-fixes.test.ts` — regression tests for
the three review threads
- `src/test/gemini-inline-photo-bounds.test.ts` — pathname and
download-deadline bounds for signed coach photos
- `src/test/gemini-inline-photo-refund.test.ts` — failed-response
cancel, in-flight abort, and stalled-body refund bounds
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` — hermetic Deno step also runs the helper
test
- `src/test/ai-coach-security.test.ts` — pin retarget
- `src/test/ai-coach-credit-recovery.test.ts` — pin retarget
- `src/test/ai-coach-output-safety.test.ts` — pin retarget, plus a
non-vacuous fetch assertion
- `src/test/ai-credit-replay-provider-boundary.test.ts` — coach pin
retarget; doctor pins unchanged

## Behavior changed

Both functions now POST to
`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/chat/completions`
with `Authorization: Bearer <GEMINI_API_KEY>`. The request body keeps
today's tools / `tool_choice` (doctor) and `response_format:
json_object` (coach). The `model` field is the native Gemini id.

| Feature | Tier | Gateway id today (still `p_model_id` for doctor) |
Native Gemini id on the wire |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `ai_doctor_review` | `standard` | `google/gemini-3-flash-preview` |
`gemini-3-flash-preview` |
| `ai_coach` | `standard` | `google/gemini-2.5-flash` |
`gemini-2.5-flash` |

Any other feature or tier fails closed as unsupported. There is no
fallback model.

### Model doc citations

Read 2026-10-11:

- OpenAI-compatible endpoint:
https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/openai — base URL
`https://generativelanguage.googleapis.com/v1beta/openai/`, chat
completions, `Authorization: Bearer $GEMINI_API_KEY`.
- Model catalog: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models — page
last updated 2026-10-09 UTC. Gemini 3 Flash endpoint
`gemini-3-flash-preview`. Gemini 2.5 Flash endpoint `gemini-2.5-flash`
(access limited to prior users; not deprecated; the page points new
projects at newer Flash models). This slice does not escalate.
- Model code page:
https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/models/gemini-2.5-flash — model
code `gemini-2.5-flash`.
- Deprecations: https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/deprecations —
`gemini-3-flash-preview` released 2025-12-17, no shutdown date
(recommended replacement `gemini-3.6-flash`, not used).
`gemini-2.5-flash` has no shutdown date.

Doctor HMAC signs the outbound native id (`WIRE_MODEL`). New receipts
use prompt contract `ai-doctor-review-prompt-v2`, so a verifier can tell
that frame from a v1 receipt signed with the provider-prefixed model id.
`p_model_id` on `ai_doctor_finalize_review` stays
`google/gemini-3-flash-preview`. Coach still does not record
`p_model_id`. A coach photo is downloaded from the already-validated
signed storage URL and sent as a bounded `data:` URL. Gemini HTTP 429 is
`upstream_credit_exhausted` in both functions; the refund reason stays
`upstream_429`.

Missing key, user-facing, unchanged:

- Doctor: HTTP 200 `{ ok: false, reason: "config" }` via
`calmFailure("config")`, log `ai-doctor-review status=config_missing
missing=gemini_api_key`. The log does not print the key.
- Coach: HTTP 500 `{ error: "AI not configured" }`.

A failed or missing-key call never reaches `ai_credit_spend`. Failures
after a successful spend still refund through the existing path.

### Cost tracking

`supabase/functions/_shared/cost.ts` re-exports
`./lib/lib/cost/index.ts`. That surface is measurement helpers, not a
price table keyed by provider and model. Left unchanged. No pricing
entries were invented.

### LOVABLE_API_KEY in production

`NOT_MEASURED`. This slice did not read secrets and did not call the
production gateway with any key. Whether the stored secret still
authorizes a completion was not measured.

Public keyless probe, 2026-10-11: `GET
https://ai.gateway.lovable.dev/v1/chat/completions` returned HTTP 405,
`Allow: POST`. A keyless `POST` of `{}` with `Content-Type:
application/json` and no `Authorization` returned HTTP 401, body title
"Missing API key". The host answers and demands a key. That does not
show whether `LOVABLE_API_KEY` still authorizes a completion. Matthew's
"inactive gateway" note is a source claim, not a measured dead host.

## Dependency inventory (read-only, head
`524d19d72264644033c1ccfae86ebff2e995742f`)

Searched `supabase/functions/**`, `src/**`, `scripts/**`,
`.github/workflows/**`, and `docs/**` for `LOVABLE_API_KEY`,
`ai.gateway.lovable.dev`, `connector-gateway.lovable.dev`,
`api.lovable.dev`, and `docs.lovable.dev`. Workflows: no matches.
`scripts/**`: no secret read and no gateway URL. The pheno smoke scripts
only treat `lovable.dev` as a hosted-hostname marker so they refuse
production.

refactor(security): one shared timing-safe compare helper for every secret check (#1002) (#1848)

# Verdant Pull Request

## Summary

Addresses #1002. I rebuilt it from the deploy tip `0107d9406` and did
**not** reuse #830's manifest.

Every secret, bearer-token and HMAC comparison now goes through one
helper, `src/lib/timingSafeCompareRules.ts`. The helper reaches Edge
functions through the repository's sync tool, not by hand-copying.

The PR is three commits; review them one at a time:
1. The helper and its tests: behavioural tests plus a static call-site
scan.
2. Call-site migration: no protocol, parsing, timestamp, replay or scope
change.
3. The regenerated `_shared/lib` mirror and manifest
(`sync-edge-shared`).

## Comparison-site audit (deploy tip)

| Site | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `src/lib/piIngestAuthRules.ts` | local XOR loop
(`constantTimeEqualHex`) | delegates to `timingSafeEqualHex`; the export
name is kept |
| `src/lib/ecowittRealIngestAuth.ts` | local `safeEqual` |
`timingSafeEqual` |
| `supabase/functions/_shared/ecowittRealIngestAuth.ts`
(**hand-maintained**) | local `safeEqual` | imports the generated
`./lib/lib/timingSafeCompareRules.ts` |
| `paddle-webhook/verifyPaddleSignature.ts` | local XOR loop |
`constantTimeEqual` delegates to `timingSafeEqual`. It stays **exact**,
with no case folding, and still compares against every `h1`. |
| `send-transactional-email/contract.ts` | local loop over accepted keys
| `timingSafeMatchesAny` |
| `preview-transactional-email/index.ts` (*newer than #830*) | `token
!== apiKey` | `timingSafeEqual` |
| `auth-email-hook/index.ts` (*newer*) | ``authHeader !== `Bearer
${apiKey}` `` | `timingSafeEqual`; the empty-key guard still runs first
|
| `edge-metrics-alert-check/index.ts` (*newer*) | `providedCronSecret
=== cronSecret` | `timingSafeEqual` |

Bridge and MCP token checks were not changed. The remaining `===` hits
are on non-secret values: ids, idempotency keys, tent scope and
`signature_verified === true`.

## Helper contract

- **`timingSafeEqual(a, b)`:** compares UTF-16 code units, with no early
exit. A length difference is folded into the result. Non-string input
never matches. `("","")` is equal, so callers keep their existing
fail-closed checks for an empty configured secret.
- **`timingSafeEqualHex(a, b)`:** lowercase is canonical. Empty or
non-hex input never matches, and the validity check is folded into the
result.
- **`timingSafeMatchesAny(candidate, accepted)`:** compares the
candidate against **every** accepted value. An empty candidate or empty
accepted value still goes through the loop and cannot match.
- **Documented as timing hygiene, not a constant-time proof.**

## Files changed

- New: `src/lib/timingSafeCompareRules.ts`.
- New tests:
  - `src/test/timing-safe-compare-rules.test.ts` (15 cases);
  - `src/test/timing-safe-compare-call-sites-static.test.ts` (12 cases).
- The 8 call-site files in the audit table above.
- Generated:
`supabase/functions/_shared/lib/lib/timingSafeCompareRules.ts`, the
mirrored `piIngestAuthRules.ts`, and `.sync-manifest.json`
(`sourceCount` 105 → 106).

## Behavior changed

Accept/reject outcomes are the same for every valid input. Only the
comparison mechanics change: no early exit, and length folding at the
sites that previously returned early.

Edge cases:
- Pi, hex digest: non-hex digests now fail by rule instead of by
mismatch.
- Paddle: comparison stays exact.
- Transactional email: an empty accepted key can never match. Before, it
could not match either, because `normalizeSecret` drops empty keys.

---

## Security checklist

- [x] No client-trusted `user_id`: unchanged.
- [x] No `service_role` introduced. Nothing in the client bundle
changed: the helper is pure and contains no secrets.
- [x] RLS: no tables touched.
- [x] No fake live or demo data.
- [x] No device-command surface.
- [x] AI Coach unchanged.
- [x] Action Queue unchanged.
- [x] Tests added.

## V0 Operating Loop impact

None.

## RLS / ownership impact

None.

## AI Coach impact

None.

## Action Queue impact

None.

## Sensor / live-data truthfulness

Not applicable. The ingest auth outcomes for Pi and EcoWitt are
unchanged.

## External-control / device-command impact

None.

---

## #1002 test checklist

| Required | Status |
|---|---|
| equal, unequal bytes, unequal lengths, empty strings, non-ASCII |
PASS: helper suite |
| valid and invalid hex, normalization | PASS |
| multi-key match at first, middle and last position, and no match;
every value evaluated | PASS: a counting Proxy proves every accepted
value is read |
| current Pi, EcoWitt, Paddle and transactional-email suites | PASS: 110
related Vitest files, 2,062 tests |
| static scan of **all** source and Edge call sites, including
`_shared/ecowittRealIngestAuth.ts` | PASS: asserts the hand-maintained
mirror is in the scan set, and that no `charCodeAt … ^ … charCodeAt`
loop exists outside the helper |
| `sync-edge-shared` produces no diff | PASS: `node
scripts/sync-edge-shared.mjs --check` and `verify-edge-shared-in-sync`
(106 files) |
| manifest hash and count parity | PASS: manifest written by the tool;
`sourceCount` 106 |
| full security and Edge gates | CI. The Deno edge tests
(`paddle-webhook/security.test.ts`,
`send-transactional-email/contract.test.ts`,
`edge-metrics-alert-check/index.test.ts`) are **NOT_MEASURED locally**
because Deno isn't installed in this sandbox. |

## Tests run

- **RED first:**
  - The helper suite failed to import.
- The static scan had **10 failing cases**: the XOR-loop scan, plus all
9 call-site import checks.
- **Targeted:** 27/27 new cases pass.
- **Related suites:** 110 files, 2,062 passed, 0 failed. They cover Pi
ingest, EcoWitt real-ingest and its edge-parity tests, Paddle and
payments-webhook static tests, transactional email, edge-shared/MCP, and
the security suites.
- **Type-check:** `bun run typecheck` shows only the 3 sandbox-only

- **Lint and format:** `eslint` 0 errors and 0 warnings on the changed
files; `prettier --check` clean.

`sync-mcp-edge-bundle --check` reports `matchedBefore: true`.
- **Full suite:** `NOT_MEASURED` locally; CI runs it in 32 shards.

## Risk / rollback notes

- **Medium-low risk.** Same accept/reject outcomes, but these are auth
paths, so the Deno and edge CI gates matter.
- **Publishing** ships the changed Edge functions.
- **Rollback:** revert the three commits. No schema, secret or protocol
changes.
- **No wall-clock timing test is included;** that is a non-goal in the
issue.

security review is welcome given the auth surface.

fix(sensors): drop hardware ids from provenance detail and allowlist the forwarding widget row (#1003) (#1855)

# Verdant Pull Request

## Summary

Closes the gaps #1163 left open on issue #1003 (#1165 and #1166 were
earlier follow-ups). Most of #1003 had already merged. An audit of
`verdant-grow-diary` found three places where credential values or
hardware ids could still reach output:

1. **Quick Log adapter and `resolveSensorSnapshotDisplay`.**
`sourceDetail` and `originalSource` carried the raw provider string, and
`SAFE_SOURCE_DETAIL_RE` (a slug regex) accepts bare and dash MACs,
UUIDs, 32-hex passkeys and MAC-bearing station ids (`gw2000a-wifi4c01`).
`SensorSnapshotCard` renders `sourceDetail`. These shapes are now
dropped. Ordinary provenance slugs are kept: `pi_bridge`, `ecowitt`,
`ggs_controller`, `home_assistant`, `esp32`.
2. **EcoWitt forwarding widget "Latest metrics" row.** The row rendered
raw `source`, `vendor` and every metric **key**, filtered only through a
denylist. It now uses the same allowlists as the copied report:
`safeSourceLabel`, `safeVendorLabel`, `safeCapturedAt`, and the new
`pickAllowedMetricKeys`. An unknown source renders as `source=invalid`.
3. **`sanitizeReportValue`** now scrubs object **keys** as well as
values, at every depth including inside arrays.

**Not changed: the metric allowlist.** The audit suggested adding
VPD/EC/pH to `ALLOWED_METRIC_KEYS`. The listener's `FIELD_MAP`
(`tools/ecowitt-testbench/ecowitt_multitent.py`) only emits `temp_f`,
`humidity_percent`, `soil_moisture_pct` and `co2_ppm`, and those are
already all allowlisted. Its channel map can also emit `soil_temp_f`;
that key is not allowlisted and is left as is.

## Files changed

- `src/lib/sensorSnapshotFreshnessRules.ts`:
  - Rejects hardware and credential shapes in `safeSourceDetail`.
  - New `safeOriginalSource`.
  - Exports `sanitizeSensorSourceDetail`.
- `src/lib/quickLogSensorSnapshotViewModelAdapter.ts`: sanitizes
`sourceDetail` at the adapter boundary.
- `src/lib/ecowittForwardingReportExport.ts`:
  - Exports the existing safe-label helpers.
  - Adds `pickAllowedMetricKeys`.
- `src/lib/ecowittLocalForwardingStatusViewModel.ts`: the widget row
uses the export allowlists.
- `src/lib/ecowittLocalForwardingStatus.ts`: `sanitizeReportValue`
scrubs keys.
- `src/test/sensor-provenance-residual-redaction-1003.test.ts`: new.

## Behavior changed

- A source detail shaped like a hardware id or credential is no longer
shown. The reading's canonical source and trust are unchanged: live
stays live and unknown stays invalid.
- The widget's latest-metrics row shows only canonical source labels,
known vendors, timestamp-shaped `captured_at` values and allowlisted
metric keys.

---

## Security checklist

- [x] No client-trusted `user_id`
- [x] No `service_role` introduced
- [x] RLS preserved (no schema or policy changes)
- [x] No fake live or demo data introduced. Unknown provenance still
fails closed to `invalid`.
- [x] No device-command surface
- [x] AI Coach unchanged
- [x] Action Queue unchanged
- [x] Tests added

## V0 Operating Loop impact

- [x] Sensor readings: reviewed. Display redaction only; freshness and
source classification are unchanged.
- [x] Dashboard snapshot, alerts, AlertDetail, ActionQueue,
ActionDetail, transitions and AI handoff: unchanged.
- [x] `src/test/v0-operating-loop-contract.test.ts` passes: 26/26.

## RLS / ownership impact

None.

## AI Coach impact

None. There is an adjacent finding outside this PR's scope:
`resolveQuickLogSensorSnapshotForAi` returns its input verbatim when the
input has no `metrics`, and returns a non-canonical `"unknown"` label.
It is flagged separately and not changed here.

## Action Queue impact

None.

## Sensor / live-data truthfulness

No reading changes trust level. Only the provenance detail string is
affected, and it is dropped, never upgraded.

## External-control / device-command impact

None.

---

## Tests run

- **RED before the fix:** the new file failed **15 of 23** on base. It
passes 23/23 after the fix.
- **Targeted:** 8 neighbouring files (adapter, view model, edge cases,
export, widget, redaction ordering, testbench static safety): **491
passed, 24 skipped**.
- **Import-overlap sweep:** the 54 test files that import any touched
module: **1157 passed, 24 skipped, 0 failed**.
- **Full suite:** not run locally; CI shards gate it.
- **`bun run typecheck`:** only the 3 known environment `Cannot find
module 'xlsx'` errors, none introduced.
- **ESLint and Prettier on changed files:** clean.
- **`verify-edge-shared-in-sync`:** OK (no mirrored files touched).

## Build / lint results

Clean.

## Risk / rollback notes

**Risk:** the hardware-id shape rule rejects any slug containing a run
of four or more hex characters that mixes digits and hex letters. A
vendor model slug like `ws2902c` would show no source detail. This fails
closed and is display-only.

**Rollback:** revert this single commit.

fix(quick-log): recover uncertain Water saves after reopen and reload (#1540)

## Summary

**Stay draft — native save/retrieve reliability.**

A structured Water save could reach `quicklog_save_event` while its
response was lost. Closing and reopening Quick Log discarded the
unresolved submission and rotated its idempotency key; entering the same
watering again could create a second logical event. A full page reload
lost the in-memory record entirely.

This change persists the original Water submission in owner-scoped
session storage before dispatch. Reopen and same-tab reload restore the
original target, key, timestamp, note, manual measurements and volume.
Retry confirms that original record before Log another becomes
available.

- Base: `3c3889855355fff8b656e51c29a41f6b26848e35`,
`verdant-grow-diary`.
- Exact head: `120c15b1dfe12e5a111f582fbf8bdf2c341c39be`.
- Six files only; no overlapping open PR implementation found.
- HOLD #1250. No merge, Publish, production APPLY, device or Action
Queue actions.

## Files changed

- `src/components/QuickLogV2Sheet.tsx`: claim/restore/confirm Water
recovery, preserve pending submissions through parent updates and
reopen, protect owner-departed async continuations, and prevent a new
logical save if confirmed-record cleanup fails.
- `src/lib/quickLogPendingWateringStore.ts`: pure validation around an
owner-scoped, versioned, exact session-storage projection.
Corrupt/unavailable storage fails closed; old completion cannot remove
another record.
- `src/lib/quickLogWateringRecoveryViewModel.ts`: restore form display
from canonical values without deriving a new target or inventing
measurements.
- `src/test/quick-log-v2-sheet-watering.test.tsx`
- `src/test/quick-log-pending-watering-store.test.ts`
- `src/test/quick-log-watering-recovery-view-model.test.ts`

## Behavior changed

Closing or reloading retains the unresolved Water record in that browser
tab. Another account cannot recover it. An earlier pending record wins
over a new competing draft. The UI states that Retry checks the original
record.

File objects cannot survive a reload: recovered attachment intent is
labelled unresolved and unavailable, and retry confirms only the
original watering record. No attachments are fabricated. A successful
save whose local recovery cleanup fails remains confirmed, but Log
another stays disabled until storage cleanup succeeds; that cleanup
retry does not dispatch another Water RPC.

The existing typed Water RPC and database idempotency contract are
unchanged. Note and Feed retain their existing behavior; related tests
run below.

## Security checklist

Reviewed against [security
checklist](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/blob/verdant-grow-diary/docs/security-checklist.md)
and [security
exceptions](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/blob/verdant-grow-diary/docs/security-exceptions.md).

- [x] No new client-trusted authorization or ownership grant. Recovery
owner ID scopes local data; the server remains authoritative.
- [x] No privileged credentials or service role added.
- [x] No schema, RLS, auth-runtime or Edge changes.
- [x] No fake live data. Synthetic ledgers/fixtures are test-only.
- [x] No device-control, Action Queue or AI changes.
- [x] Focused regression and storage tests included.

## V0 Operating Loop impact

Quick Log Water save/retry now survives close/reopen and same-tab
reload. The target and canonical manual source/measurements stay frozen.
Other sensor, alert, Action Queue, and AI surfaces are unchanged.
`v0-operating-loop-contract.test.ts` was not rerun for this head; no
separate pass is claimed.

## RLS / ownership impact

None on the server. No `supabase/` files changed. Owner departure
prevents late upload/write continuations from starting under a new
account. Storage is local to the existing browser session/tab.

## AI Coach impact

None.

## Action Queue impact

None.

## Sensor / live-data truthfulness

Recovered optional metrics remain canonical manual readings with the
original capture time. Empty values remain empty. Browser proof typed
77°F and 55% RH and observed the same retry payload containing
`temperature_c: 25`, `humidity_pct: 55`, `source: manual` and the
original timestamp.

## External-control / device-command impact

None.

## Tests run

**PASS — 365 passed / 0 failed / 0 skipped, 16 files**, including **113
focused Water tests**: component 35, recovery store 75, restored-form
view model 3.

Coverage includes accepted-save/lost-reply recovery, close/reopen, full
remount, parent-target changes, A→B→A account isolation, blocked
storage, exact clear, confirmed-save cleanup failure, and held-upload
owner departure, plus related Note, Feed, attachment, target,
temperature and typed-writer regressions.

The initial real-component/typed-writer diagnostic reproduced two
accepted logical records after reopen with a new key. The expanded
pre-fix suite had **25 passing / 9 intentionally failing / 0 skipped**
tests. The old unsafe key-rotation expectation was replaced with
confirmation-before-new-entry behavior.

Command (existing dependencies; Bun unavailable, Node 24.15.0 / Vitest
4.1.11):

```text
node node_modules/vitest/vitest.mjs run src/test/quick-log-v2-sheet-watering.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-pending-watering-store.test.ts src/test/quick-log-watering-recovery-view-model.test.ts src/test/quick-log-v2-sheet-feeding.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-v2-exact-recovery.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-v2-note-sync.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-pending-note-store.test.ts src/test/quick-log-v2-sheet-photo-gate.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-temperature-unit-entry.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-v2-response-check-chips-runtime.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-v2-context-states.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-v2-sheet-watering-volume-defaults.test.tsx src/test/quick-log-target-resolution-rules.test.ts src/test/write-quick-log-watering-typed-event.test.ts src/test/quick-log-v2-static-safety.test.ts src/test/quick-log-v2-refresh-static-safety.test.ts --maxWorkers=2 --reporter=json
```

**PASS — 2 actual Chromium UI walkthroughs / 0 failed:** close/reopen
and page reload. Each accepted the original save in an intercepted fake
backend, dropped the response, then confirmed exactly the same RPC
payload on retry: **2 requests, 1 logical record, 0 unexpected writes, 0
page errors** per case. All nonlocal/nonfixture hosts were blocked;
fixture backend was `https://water-proof.supabase.invalid`. This is
client/UI evidence, **not real database or production acceptance**. The
local script and JSON receipt are retained in the Codex handoff.

## Build / lint results

- **PASS with warnings:** ESLint on six changed files, **0 errors / 3
hook-dependency warnings**.
- **FAIL, unchanged baseline:** full `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`,
**43 diagnostics**. Output SHA-256 matches the recorded unmodified
baseline exactly:
`DF48DD82F8E56BB48B8E0414D1DEA62F18789EBAECC07A0C1A237A4CBD7F6F3F`. Two

before the final run.
- **PASS:** `git diff --cached --check`; six intended files only.

proof locally. Existing native CI proof does not yet contain this
typed-Water recovery case.
- **NOT_MEASURED:** production deployment/acceptance and independent
Blue Dream review.

## Risk / rollback notes

Recovery survives the current browser tab/session; it is not
cross-device or durable after session storage is cleared. Files cannot
be reconstructed after reload, and their unresolved status is explicit.
This does not prove atomicity or deduplication of separate media
companion writes.

The recovery validator intentionally uses the same numeric boundaries as
the typed writer without importing its live-client side effects; future
writer-contract changes must keep the recovery projection aligned.

Rollback is a code revert of these six files. No migration or production
data change occurred. Keep draft for independent review; do not merge or
Publish.

fix(auth): consume OAuth hash tokens on / and honor post-auth redirect (#1299)

## Summary
Live FAIL leftover after #1293 (hop PASS): Google SSO return lands on
`/` with `#access_token=...` (and related hash params), but the SPA did
not reliably consume the hash into a Supabase `sessionStorage` session.
`OAuthPostAuthRedirect` therefore never saw `user`, and pending
`redirectTo` was not honored.

## Fix
1. **`oauthHashSessionConsumeRules`** — parse OAuth hash fragments
(`access_token` + `refresh_token`, or `error=`). Fail closed on
malformed/missing tokens (no invented sessions). Clear the hash via
`history.replaceState` without a full reload.
2. **`AuthProvider`** — on bootstrap, `consumeOAuthHashSessionIfPresent`
→ `supabase.auth.setSession` **before** the initial `getSession`, so
session → `user` → existing `OAuthPostAuthRedirect` ordering holds.
3. **Tests** — unit coverage for parse / reject / clear / consume;
static wiring that AuthProvider owns the consume path (does not edit
auto-generated Lovable shim or supabase client).

Author: Claude
Message:
fix(reports): redact header-prefixed assignments with unlabelled names

Copilot raised this on #1187 and it is real — confirmed by execution on
9f739b4 before any change was made.

The credential-labelled assignment rule added earlier in this PR only
protects NAMEs carrying a keyword. Behind a header prefix, an unlabelled
NAME was still consumed by the bearer rule and its VALUE left behind:

  bearer SOME_PLAIN_NAME=REDACTED -> [redacted]=REDACTED

That is output which LOOKS sanitized while the credential survives — worse
than no redaction, because nothing signals it to a reader.

The same probe found a second leak Copilot did not report: this module had
no Authorization rule of any kind, so

  Authorization: SOME_PLAIN_NAME=REDACTED

passed through COMPLETELY unredacted. Fixing the bearer half alone would
have shipped a leak already measured, so both are closed by one rule.

The fix takes Copilot's suggested direction: match the whole assignment
behind a credential header rather than adding a generic uppercase rule. The
header is the discriminator that makes this safe in a user-facing grow
report — it fires only after bearer/Authorization, so bare telemetry is
untouched. Verified across 12 benign inputs, all byte-identical, including
"Notes: light bearer arm adjusted to height=90cm", where the rule correctly
declines because the assignment does not immediately follow the name.

Also adds a partial-redaction fence as its own property: a placeholder in
the output while the secret is still present means a rule fired and
destroyed only part of the span. That is the shape of every defect in this
class and the one failure mode a reader cannot spot by eye.

RED before the fix: 7 failed | 70 passed (77). GREEN after: 77 passed (77).
Post-grow sweep 38 files, 445 passed | 16 skipped. tsc clean, eslint clean.
Module is not mirrored into supabase/functions/_shared — no edge-sync
obligation.

# Verdant Pull Request

> Draft only — no ready, merge, publish, or production SQL.

## Summary

**Third instance of the redaction-ordering defect class**, in
`postGrowReportRules.ts`. Unlike the first two
([#1185](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/pull/1185),
[#1184](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/pull/1184))
this one was found by a **deliberate audit** of every module carrying a
secret-pattern list, not by a reviewer tripping over it.

Two distinct findings, both **proven by execution** on the untouched tip
`f9f4d11`.

### 1. Ordering — the same consuming mechanism

The `bearer` rule ran before the `BridgeToken` assignment rule, so it
consumed the variable NAME and left the value behind:

```text
bearer BridgeToken=REDACTED   ->  [redacted]=REDACTED
Bearer BridgeToken: REDACTED  ->  [redacted]: REDACTED
```

### 2. Coverage — worse, and NOT fixable by reordering

```text
SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=REDACTED     ->  SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=REDACTED
```

**Entirely unredacted.** Two causes, both verified:

- `\bservice_role\b` **cannot match inside `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`** — `_` is
a word character, so the trailing `\b` fails (confirmed directly:
`false`).
- This module had **no credential-assignment rule of any kind** to act
as a backstop (verified: 0 matches for a generic assignment pattern).

Reordering alone would not have fixed this. It needed a new rule.

## The design decision worth reviewing

**I deliberately did NOT use the generic `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,}=` rule**
that the two sibling modules use.

This helper renders a **user-facing grow report** and its contract is
*"Preserves prose."* Grow telemetry uses exactly the same uppercase
`NAME=value` shape, so a generic rule would redact `VPD=1.2`,
`PPFD=800`, `EC=1.8` — destroying real report content in the name of
security. The sibling modules handle debug payloads, where that trade is
acceptable; here it is not.

Instead the new rule **requires a credential label in the NAME**, which
closes the leak without touching report data.

**No new breadth beyond that intent, proven** — nine benign inputs,
including uppercase telemetry, a mixed prose-and-telemetry sentence, and
plain prose, are **byte-identical** before and after:

```text
VPD=1.2                                            -> unchanged
Week 6 canopy stable; runoff EC=1.8 and VPD=1.2.   -> unchanged
harvest_weight=412                                 -> unchanged
```

## Files changed

- `src/lib/postGrowReportRules.ts` — one rule moved, one rule added,
ordering comment marking it load-bearing
- `src/test/post-grow-report-pdf-export.test.tsx` — 14 tests: 3
header-prefix, 4 labelled-assignment, 7 benign-content fences

**Not mirrored** into `supabase/functions/_shared` — checked, so no
edge-sync obligation. No new file, no schema, no SQL.

## Security checklist

- [x] No client-trusted `user_id`
- [x] No `service_role` introduced in frontend or Edge Functions
- [x] RLS preserved — no schema, SQL, or policy change
- [x] No fake live / demo data introduced or surfaced as real
- [x] No new device-command / external-control surface
- [x] AI Coach unchanged
- [x] Action Queue unchanged
- [x] Tests added/updated when behavior changes

## V0 Operating Loop impact

None. Report-export redaction only; no loop surface touched.

## RLS / ownership impact

None. Migrations remain **NOT applied**.

## AI Coach impact

None.

## Action Queue impact

None.

## Sensor / live-data truthfulness

No classification, freshness or source-label logic is touched. The
change is strictly about what is **redacted** from an exported report —
and specifically about *not* over-redacting real sensor values, which
the benign fences pin.

## External-control / device-command impact

None.

## Tests run

| Stage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| RED — new tests vs. **untouched** module | **7 failed / 60 passed
(67)** |
| GREEN — after the fix | **67 passed (67)** |
| post-grow + report sweep | **92 files, 839 passed / 0 failed** |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` on changed files | clean |

## Risk / rollback

**Low-moderate.** One rule moved, one added. The realistic failure mode
is *over*-redaction of report content, which is why seven benign fences
pin telemetry and prose as byte-identical. Rollback is a single-commit
revert; reverting re-opens both leaks above.

## Out of scope

The **shared ordering contract** — the durable remedy.
`proofReportRedactionRules.ts` already implements the correct order
(auth headers → pairs → bare keywords) and documents the hazard in its
own comments; three modules independently got it wrong. A lint rule or
shared contract preventing a fourth is a separate slice and is **not**
attempted here.

# Verdant Pull Request

> Draft only — no ready, merge, publish, or production SQL.

## Summary

**Third instance of the redaction-ordering defect class**, in
`postGrowReportRules.ts`. Unlike the first two
([#1185](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/pull/1185),
[#1184](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/pull/1184))
this one was found by a **deliberate audit** of every module carrying a
secret-pattern list, not by a reviewer tripping over it.

Two distinct findings, both **proven by execution** on the untouched tip
`f9f4d11`.

### 1. Ordering — the same consuming mechanism

The `bearer` rule ran before the `BridgeToken` assignment rule, so it
consumed the variable NAME and left the value behind:

```text
bearer BridgeToken=REDACTED   ->  [redacted]=REDACTED
Bearer BridgeToken: REDACTED  ->  [redacted]: REDACTED
```

### 2. Coverage — worse, and NOT fixable by reordering

```text
SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=REDACTED     ->  SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=REDACTED
```

**Entirely unredacted.** Two causes, both verified:

- `\bservice_role\b` **cannot match inside `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`** — `_` is
a word character, so the trailing `\b` fails (confirmed directly:
`false`).
- This module had **no credential-assignment rule of any kind** to act
as a backstop (verified: 0 matches for a generic assignment pattern).

Reordering alone would not have fixed this. It needed a new rule.

## The design decision worth reviewing

**I deliberately did NOT use the generic `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,}=` rule**
that the two sibling modules use.

This helper renders a **user-facing grow report** and its contract is
*"Preserves prose."* Grow telemetry uses exactly the same uppercase
`NAME=value` shape, so a generic rule would redact `VPD=1.2`,
`PPFD=800`, `EC=1.8` — destroying real report content in the name of
security. The sibling modules handle debug payloads, where that trade is
acceptable; here it is not.

Instead the new rule **requires a credential label in the NAME**, which
closes the leak without touching report data.

**No new breadth beyond that intent, proven** — nine benign inputs,
including uppercase telemetry, a mixed prose-and-telemetry sentence, and
plain prose, are **byte-identical** before and after:

```text
VPD=1.2                                            -> unchanged
Week 6 canopy stable; runoff EC=1.8 and VPD=1.2.   -> unchanged
harvest_weight=412                                 -> unchanged
```

## Files changed

- `src/lib/postGrowReportRules.ts` — one rule moved, one rule added,
ordering comment marking it load-bearing
- `src/test/post-grow-report-pdf-export.test.tsx` — 14 tests: 3
header-prefix, 4 labelled-assignment, 7 benign-content fences

**Not mirrored** into `supabase/functions/_shared` — checked, so no
edge-sync obligation. No new file, no schema, no SQL.

- [x] No `service_role` introduced in frontend or Edge Functions
- [x] RLS preserved — no schema, SQL, or policy change
- [x] No fake live / demo data introduced or surfaced as real
- [x] No new device-command / external-control surface
- [x] AI Coach unchanged
- [x] Action Queue unchanged
- [x] Tests added/updated when behavior changes

None. Report-export redaction only; no loop surface touched.

## RLS / ownership impact

None. Migrations remain **NOT applied**.

## AI Coach impact

None.

## Action Queue impact

None.

## Sensor / live-data truthfulness

No classification, freshness or source-label logic is touched. The
change is strictly about what is **redacted** from an exported report —
and specifically about *not* over-redacting real sensor values, which
the benign fences pin.

## External-control / device-command impact

None.

## Tests run

| Stage | Result |
| --- | --- |
| RED — new tests vs. **untouched** module | **7 failed / 60 passed
(67)** |
| GREEN — after the fix | **67 passed (67)** |
| post-grow + report sweep | **92 files, 839 passed / 0 failed** |
| `tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit` | clean |
| `eslint` on changed files | clean |

## Risk / rollback

**Low-moderate.** One rule moved, one added. The realistic failure mode
is *over*-redaction of report content, which is why seven benign fences
pin telemetry and prose as byte-identical. Rollback is a single-commit
revert; reverting re-opens both leaks above.

## Out of scope

The **shared ordering contract** — the durable remedy.
`proofReportRedactionRules.ts` already implements the correct order
(auth headers → pairs → bare keywords) and documents the hazard in its
own comments; three modules independently got it wrong. A lint rule or
shared contract preventing a fourth is a separate slice and is **not**
attempted here.

## Summary

**Third instance of the redaction-ordering defect class**, in
`postGrowReportRules.ts`. Unlike the first two
([#1185](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/pull/1185),
[#1184](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/pull/1184))
this one was found by a **deliberate audit** of every module carrying a
secret-pattern list, not by a reviewer tripping over it.

Two distinct findings, both **proven by execution** on the untouched tip
`f9f4d11`.

### 1. Ordering — the same consuming mechanism

The `bearer` rule ran before the `BridgeToken` assignment rule, so it
consumed the variable NAME and left the value behind:

```text
bearer BridgeToken=REDACTED   ->  [redacted]=REDACTED
Bearer BridgeToken: REDACTED  ->  [redacted]: REDACTED
```

### 2. Coverage — worse, and NOT fixable by reordering

```text
SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=REDACTED     ->  SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=REDACTED
```

**Entirely unredacted.** Two causes, both verified:

- `\bservice_role\b` **cannot match inside `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`** — `_` is
a word character, so the trailing `\b` fails (confirmed directly:
`false`).
- This module had **no credential-assignment rule of any kind** to act
as a backstop (verified: 0 matches for a generic assignment pattern).

Reordering alone would not have fixed this. It needed a new rule.

## The design decision worth reviewing

**I deliberately did NOT use the generic `[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{2,}=` rule**
that the two sibling modules use.

This helper renders a **user-facing grow report** and its contract is
*"Preserves prose."* Grow telemetry uses exactly the same uppercase
`NAME=value` shape, so a generic rule would redact `VPD=1.2`,
`PPFD=800`, `EC=1.8` — destroying real report content in the name of
security. The sibling modules handle debug payloads, where that trade is
acceptable; here it is not.

Instead the new rule **requires a credential label in the NAME**, which
closes the leak without touching report data.

**No new breadth beyond that intent, proven** — nine benign inputs,
including uppercase telemetry, a mixed prose-and-telemetry sentence, and
plain prose, are **byte-identical** before and after:

```text

Week 6 canopy stable; runoff EC=1.8 and VPD=1.2.   -> unchanged
harvest_weight=412                                 -> unchanged
```

fix(sensors): fail closed on unknown provenance and allowlist forwarding-report export (#1003) (#1163)

# Verdant Pull Request

## Summary

Closes the two sensor-truth holes of issue
[#1003](https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/issues/1003),
both proven live on tip (`11b0ca6`) before any code was written:

1. **Unknown provenance could become `live`.**
`quickLogSensorSnapshotViewModelAdapter.mapSource` promoted *any*
unknown provider string to canonical `"live"` whenever upstream
freshness was `"fresh"` — so a fresh unknown-source snapshot produced an
attachable view-model payload stamped `source: "live"`. `mapSource` now
delegates to the repo's sanctioned alias table
(`normalizeSensorSource`): canonical vocabulary passes through, reviewed
aliases map (`sim`→demo, `diary`→manual, first-party `pi_bridge`→live),
everything else normalizes to `"invalid"`. Freshness is never consulted.
2. **Forwarding-report export fallback bypassed sanitization, and
patterns matched labels, not values.** `ecowittForwardingReportExport`'s
status-fallback envelope exported `captured_at`/`source`/`vendor` raw.
Both `latest_metrics` paths now shape/value-allowlist at the module
boundary (timestamp shape for `captured_at`/`generated_at`; canonical
source vocabulary with unknown→`"invalid"`, never echoed, never live;
enumerated first-party vendor labels — a shape regex is insufficient
because station ids, bare MACs, and 32-hex passkeys are all
slug-shaped). `serializeSanitizedForwardingReport` re-walks the report
through the exact declared shape (recursive output allowlist).
`SECRET_PATTERNS` now redacts credential **values**: separated and
bare-12-hex MACs, 32+-hex passkey material with hex lookarounds
(`0x…`/`PASSKEY_…`/`sbp_…` prefixes cannot evade), UUIDs, `sk-` keys,
and env `NAME=value` pairs — while plain long numbers (epoch timestamps)
stay untouched.

One coherence follow-through: with the fail-closed adapter, a legacy
transport-labeled row (canonical resolver: usable/fresh_non_live) would
have rendered a contradictory "invalid" advisory under a "Usable" pill
on the Quick Log strip; that exact combination is suppressed (every
stale/invalid/demo/missing advisory on a non-usable card still renders).

Verdicts per issue #1003's gate, all `established fact` from
reading/executing tip code: the hole was **live**, not NOT_APPLICABLE —
the #687-era test even documented the promotion as intended ("unknown
provider only becomes live when upstream freshness is fresh").

## Files changed

- `src/lib/quickLogSensorSnapshotViewModelAdapter.ts` — fail-closed
source mapping via `normalizeSensorSource`
- `src/lib/ecowittForwardingReportExport.ts` — envelope allowlists on
both paths; recursive output-allowlist serializer
- `src/lib/ecowittLocalForwardingStatus.ts` — `SECRET_PATTERNS`
credential-value rules
- `src/components/QuickLogSensorSnapshotStrip.tsx` —
advisory/canonical-pill coherence suppression (narrow, commented)
- `src/test/quick-log-sensor-snapshot-view-model-adapter.test.ts` — new
(12 tests)
- `src/test/ecowitt-forwarding-report-export.test.ts` — new (17 tests;
credential **values** injected on top-level, nested, fallback, and
post-build tamper paths; forbidden fields present in fixtures and proven
absent from object and serialized output)
- `src/test/quicklog-sensor-snapshot-strip-render.test.tsx` — one added
coherence test

## Behavior changed

- Quick Log view-model/advisory path: unknown provider strings resolve
to the explicit untrusted state (`effectiveSource: "invalid"`, never
attachable) instead of `live`-when-fresh. `pi_bridge` — the one active
production writer of a provider-string source
(`supabase/functions/pi-ingest-readings`) — keeps its sanctioned live
alias, so no genuine first-party telemetry demotes. Legacy webhook-era
transport labels (`ecowitt`, `mqtt`, …; population in production
`NOT_MEASURED`) resolve as invalid in this view-model, matching the
strict resolver's existing `LIVE_SOURCES = {"live"}` fence; the
canonical badge path is untouched.
- Forwarding debug report: unknown source labels export as `"invalid"`
instead of being echoed; vendor values outside the enumerated
first-party set export as `null`; non-timestamp
`captured_at`/`generated_at` export as `null`; free-form error fields
additionally redact MAC/hex/UUID/`sk-`/env-pair values.
- No schema, RLS, edge-function, migration, or route changes. No
behavior change for canonical `live | manual | csv | demo | stale |
invalid` rows.

---

## Security checklist

Reviewed against
[`docs/security-checklist.md`](../docs/security-checklist.md).

- [x] No client-trusted `user_id`
- [x] No `service_role` introduced in frontend or Edge Functions
- [x] RLS preserved on every touched table (no schema/policy changes)
- [x] No fake live / demo data introduced or surfaced as real — this PR
removes a fake-live path
- [x] No new device-command / external-control surface introduced
- [x] AI Coach unchanged
- [x] Action Queue unchanged
- [x] Tests added/updated when behavior changes

## V0 Operating Loop impact

- [x] Sensor readings (manual ingest, freshness, source) — ingest
unchanged; client-side provenance labeling reviewed (this PR's subject)
- [x] Dashboard latest environment snapshot — unchanged
- [x] Environment alerts (derivation rules) — unchanged
- [x] Alert persistence (`alerts`, `alert_events`) — unchanged
- [x] AlertDetail — unchanged
- [x] ActionQueue — unchanged
- [x] ActionDetail — unchanged
- [x] Action Queue transitions (approve / reject / complete / cancel) —
unchanged
- [x] AI Coach → Action Queue handoff — unchanged
- [x] `src/test/v0-operating-loop-contract.test.ts` still passes — 26/26

## RLS / ownership impact

None.

## AI Coach impact

None.

## Action Queue impact

None.

## Sensor / live-data truthfulness

This PR's subject: unknown/non-allowlisted provider strings can no
longer be labeled `live` by freshness alone anywhere in the Quick Log
view-model chain, and the operator forwarding report can no longer
export unsanitized envelope fields or credential values. Stale/missing
handling is unchanged; nothing untrusted renders healthy.

## External-control / device-command impact

None.

---

## Tests run

- [x] New suites RED-proven against the pre-fix tree **with the final
test files**: adapter **4 failed / 8 passed**, export **7 failed / 10
passed**; strip coherence test **1 failed / 11 passed** against the
intermediate state it guards (new adapter, no suppression). All 41/41
green post-fix.
- [x] Broad targeted sweep (`src/test/ecowitt-*`, `quicklog-*`,
`quick-log-*`, `sensor-*`, v0 contract, wording guardrails): **Tests
6298 passed | 3 skipped (6301)**, 0 failures (skips
pre-existing/conditional).
- [x] `bun run typecheck` — clean
- [x] `bunx eslint` on all changed files — clean
- [x] `bun run build` — succeeds incl. pre/postbuild SEO gates
- Full 32-shard suite: left to CI (repo convention).

## Build / lint results

Clean. Pre-commit ran prettier, eslint --fix, full `tsc --noEmit`,
docs-safety asserts, and its 67-test hook suite — all green.

## Risk / rollback notes

- Rollback = revert the single commit; no data or schema effects.
- `inference` — legacy webhook-era rows still carrying transport labels
in `sensor_readings.source` (trigger-legal; production population
`NOT_MEASURED` from this session) now read as invalid in the Quick Log
view-model path. That is the fail-closed direction issue #1003 mandates;
the canonical badge already treated them as non-live.
- Adversarially reviewed pre-push by three independent verification
passes (correctness / security completeness / test soundness); both
security findings raised there (vendor shape-regex bypass via station
ids and bare MACs; `\b`-anchored hex patterns evaded by
`0x`/`PASSKEY_`/`sbp_` prefixes) are fixed and probe-tested in this
diff.
- Recorded follow-ups, deliberately **not** in this minimal slice: (1)
`metric_keys` renders unsanitized key **names** in the local forwarding
widget (values are sanitized; the clipboard export never includes
`metric_keys`); (2) `safeSourceDetail`'s shape gate in
`sensorSnapshotFreshnessRules` admits hex/UUID/MAC-shaped strings onto
display models other chains render; (3) the EcoWitt validation panel's
`redacted_raw_payload` export path redacts by key patterns only (misses
`PASSKEY`/`mac`/`ip`/`station_id` values); (4)
`sensorDiagnosticsExportRules` serializes the raw webhook response body
with `vbt_`-only redaction. Each is outside this PR's two boundaries.
- Known inherited reds expected on this PR, dispositioned on every
recent PR in `docs/agents/CURRENT_STATE.md`: `Supabase Preview` 42P07
replay (non-required) and the owner-credential Quick Log smoke.

## Behavior changed

- Production source initializes only Paddle sandbox.
- Live-class and malformed tokens resolve unavailable on every host.
- Paddle script loading, price resolution, auth/session/overlay work,
and legacy Upgrade initialization require exact sandbox authorization.
- Public pricing and the payment banner explicitly identify sandbox/test
checkout and state that no real charges occur.
- The tracked production client token is verified as **sandbox-class**.
Its value is intentionally never printed or recorded here.

## Settings transition / operational caveat

This PR changes source policy only; it does **not** mutate hosting,
edge, webhook, secret, or catalog settings.

For sandbox checkout to operate after publish, the operator-managed
environment must remain coordinated around sandbox: the public client
token must be sandbox-class, `PAYMENTS_ENVIRONMENT` and the legacy
`PADDLE_ENVIRONMENT` must resolve to `sandbox`, and the API key, webhook
signing secret, and catalog/price identifiers must all be the matching
sandbox resources. A mismatch fails closed as checkout unavailable; it
cannot fall through to live checkout.

A future live transition requires a separate explicit authorization and
one coordinated change across source policy, client/server settings,
secrets, catalog IDs, webhook verification, entitlement proof, and live
smoke evidence. Swapping only a token or environment flag is not a valid
launch procedure.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: Verdant
Message:
fix(analytics): restore route and SEO release contracts (#697)

## Summary

Provides TanStack Query's router-owned `QueryClient` to the root
application tree, so authenticated routes can safely mount `AppSidebar`
and its `useHasRole` query.

## Root cause

The router context carried a `queryClient`, but `RootComponent` never
rendered `QueryClientProvider`. Every authenticated route nested under
`_app` mounts `AppShell` and `AppSidebar`, so React Query hooks could
fall into `RootErrorBoundary` before the page rendered.

## Changes

- Wrap the root provider tree in `QueryClientProvider` using the
existing router-owned client.
- Add a static contract test for the provider boundary.
- Add a mocked-browser regression that verifies the authenticated shell
mounts without the root error boundary.

## Validation

- `bun run typecheck` — passed.
- Targeted Vitest contract test — 1 passed (temporary config only
because the repository config imports undeclared
`@vitejs/plugin-react-swc`).
- Targeted mocked Chromium regression — 1 passed using locally installed
Chrome in a disposable test config.
- Touched-file ESLint semantic rules — passed with only
`prettier/prettier` disabled; the regular formatter reports Windows
CRLF-only noise across all three files.

No schema, RLS, auth-policy, data, or deployment changes.

- The new mocked authenticated-shell test passes in CI.
- The existing full Symptom Check interaction still fails because
`/plants/:id` renders the Plants index instead of Plant Detail. That is
a separate routing defect exposed after the provider crash is fixed; it
is intentionally not bundled into this PR.
- Repository-wide lockfile and ESLint gates are already red on the
target branch (missing required `package-lock.json` and broad
pre-existing lint findings). They are outside this focused repair.
