Build 7: Skill Evaluation Harness and Promotion Pipeline (Gate A remains open) (#616)

> **WARNING — Gate A remains OPEN**
>
> The known code blockers are implemented on current head
`91f4b3d2c4af44ce44278c92b76f13b850e5e075`: P1 A/B, canonical fired-rule
shapes, source-revision pinning, the exact `observation_only` invariant,
fail-closed PlantContextCompilation/decision-regeneration gating, and
the `--json-only` artifact inconsistency.
> Build 7 still marks policy decisions `consistency_only`;
exposure-increasing promotion is blocked until Build 8 can produce
`regenerated`.
> Do **not** merge or begin Build 8 until current-head CI completes and
two independent reviews of this exact head report no P0/P1 safety
defects.

Three reviewable commits; **squash-merge** so mainline stays one logical
commit per build.

## Governing rule

> No evaluation status, score, promotion decision, or human-facing
report is trustworthy until every required binding verifies.

The failure mode of an evaluation harness is not a wrong number — it is
an attractive report that is not about the thing it claims to describe.
A green report bound to last week’s manifest is worse than no report,
because it is believed. So the binding layer shipped in commit 1, before
any executor or scoring existed.

## Binding integrity

**SHA-256 over a typed envelope.** FNV is not accepted for verification
anywhere: a non-cryptographic hash is fine for a cache key and unfit for
a release gate.

**The browser boundary is physical, not conditional.** `src/lib` owns
the envelope, the required-binding policy and the fail-closed verifier;
a Node-only adapter under `scripts/lib` owns the hash and injects it. A
conditional runtime import would have hidden the bundle hazard rather
than removed it. The property that makes this right: **a caller without
a `DigestFn` cannot construct a binding at all** — unbound evaluation is
unrepresentable, the same shape as Build 1 making device execution
unrepresentable. A source scan asserts `src/` imports `node:crypto`
nowhere; the production build passing confirms it.

**Domain separation is framed, not concatenated.** `artifact_type` and
`serializer_version` sit inside the hashed bytes, so the same payload
under a different type is a different digest and a manifest digest can
never verify as a corpus digest. A test pins that `"ab"+"c"` and
`"a"+"bc"` stay distinct.

**Fail-closed everywhere:** unknown algorithm, unknown envelope version,
unsupported serializer, malformed hex, wrong artifact type, missing
binding, digest mismatch. A relabelled algorithm is never silently
reinterpreted.

## Two axes, kept apart

```
Manifest lifecycle     = what the registered skill DECLARES itself to be
Evaluation progression = what evidence the harness has VERIFIED
```

Build 4’s `SKILL_LIFECYCLE_STATES` is untouched.
`PROGRESSION_TO_MANIFEST_LIFECYCLE` maps the four gate states —
`schema_valid`, `static_safety_passed`, `golden_cases_passed`,
`expert_reviewed` — to **`null`**: they authorize no manifest
transition, because a golden case passing is a property of a *report*,
not something a manifest can declare about itself.

Promotion emits a decision and cannot change anything. No writes, no
registry, no persistence — asserted by test.

## Honest metrics

Every rate carries numerator, denominator and status. A rate with no
applicable cases reports `not_measured` with a **null** value, never
100%. Confidence checks are **conformance** to a fixture band, never
calibration — the field name is pinned by test.

## Validation (historical, preserved)

| Gate | Result |
| --- | --- |
| Typecheck | pass |
| Lint (touched) | pass |
| Build 7 targeted suite | 6 files, **105 passed**, 0 failed |
| Self-test CLI | 14 cases, 14 passed, 0 safety failures, exit 0 |
| Artifact validation | 0 violations |
| Static safety | 8 files, 176 passed |
| Build 1-6 regression | 10 files, 562 passed |
| Production build | exit 0 |
| Full suite | **exit 1** — 21 failed / 22202 passed / 57 skipped |

### On the full suite

It exits **nonzero**, so it is not green and I am not calling it green.

The 21 failures across 12 files are **pre-existing and unrelated**,
established by evidence rather than assumption: checking out `main` and
running the same 12 files reproduces **exactly 12 failed files and 21
failed tests**. Build 7 contributes zero. They are the known
Windows-local artifacts — scan guards using forward-slash path
separators, and TZ-sensitive date tests; CI is Linux and UTC.

The known `OneTentLiveProof.tsx` timer leak **did not fire in this run**
(zero unhandled errors). It is timing-dependent and remains a separate
defect. It is not suppressed, worked around, or touched here.

The Build 7 CI gate is deliberately independent so it stays trustworthy
regardless.

## Scope

No schema, RLS, auth, Edge Function, Supabase write, UI, provider call,
Action Queue write, or device-control change. No production skill added
or promoted.

Six of the spec’s 20 self-test categories are deliberately absent from
the CLI fixture set — the binding-mismatch, malformed-contract and
nondeterminism negatives cannot live in a green fixture run. They are
covered directly in the bindings and evaluator suites.

**Gate A remains OPEN.**
The known implementation blockers are closed on
`91f4b3d2c4af44ce44278c92b76f13b850e5e075`.
PlantContextCompilation/decision regeneration is an explicit Build 8
boundary with a machine-readable fail-closed gate: Build 7 emits
`consistency_only`, and exposure-increasing promotion requires
`regenerated`. Current-head CI and two consecutive independent clean
reviews of this exact head are still required.

Build 3: deterministic Plant Context Compiler (engine-only) (#610)

## Build 3 — Plant Context Compiler

`compilePlantContextBundle` assembles one compact, time-aligned context
bundle from rows the caller already fetched, plus
`summarizeRecentActions`, `summarizeSensorWindow`,
`identifyContextGaps`, and `buildCompactTimeline`. Pure: no UI, no
schema, no writes, no model calls, no `Date.now()` — `nowMs` is
injected.

### The naming decision (the central finding)
A 5-agent reuse map found `compilePlantContextFromRows` **already
exported twice with incompatible return shapes** —
`aiDoctorContextCompiler.ts` (Phase 1:
`recent_grow_events`/`sensor_groups`/`averages_7d`) and
`aiDoctorEngine.ts` (legacy: `recent_actions`/`sensor_averages_7d`) —
and `aiDoctorEnginePhase1Foundation.ts` documents in-code that it
renamed *its* compiler specifically to escape that collision.
`PlantContextPayload` and `SensorSourceTag` are forked too (one variant
is missing `demo` entirely).

So Build 3's "one canonical context bundle" exit gate is a
**de-duplication problem, not a greenfield one**. This module therefore
takes a distinct entry-point name and, rather than adding a fourth
bundle shape, **embeds the canonical Build 1 `PlantContextBundle`**
(schema-validated) as its identity core with skill-facing sections
around it.

### Composition, not a second rule system
- **Row shapes reused** from `aiDoctorContextCompiler` — the de facto
row contract callers already speak.
- **Timeline ordering + double-write dedup** via `mergeTimelineSources`,
the only rule that merges `diary_entries` and `grow_events`. The repo
has ~6 competing comparators; this adds none.
- **All sensor summarization routes through the Build 2 truth gate.**
The legacy `averages_7d` path never sees unit normalization,
suspicious-value nulling, or conflict detection, so it is deliberately
not reused.
- **Windows**: the sketch's suggested 72h "immediate" window had *no
owner* in the repo, while `AI_DOCTOR_SNAPSHOT_FRESH_HOURS` (48h) is
exported and test-pinned — so the established value wins, per the spec's
"only if the repository has no established values". 14d/7d match the
three private legacy copies and are **exported here for the first time**
so those can converge later instead of forking a fourth.
- **Timezone-less timestamps rejected**, matching the Sensor Truth
Gate's determinism rule.

### Honesty rules (test-pinned)
Missing context is reported, never inferred · grower actions are never
invented (an absent action is a stated gap, not "not done") ·
invalid/stale/demo readings are warned and excluded from healthy
evidence, never averaged in · conflicting readings stay visible as
conflicts · the canonical snapshot is stamped only from gate-usable
values, else omitted entirely · raw payloads never enter the bundle.

### Verification
`tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` ✅ · 25 new tests ✅ · `action-queue-safety`,
`cross-ingest-vpd-regression`, `ai-doctor-engine-core-static-safety`,
`sensor-truth-gate` scanners ✅ (159 total) · Prettier + ESLint ✅.

### Exit gate
Skills consume one canonical bundle without UI knowledge and without
calling Supabase from presentation components.

Build 2: deterministic Sensor Truth Gate (engine-only) (#609)

## Build 2 — Sensor Truth Gate

The deterministic pre-AI telemetry gate for Verdant Skill Runtime v1:
[`src/lib/sensorTruthGateRules.ts`](../blob/claude/verdant-sensor-truth-gate/src/lib/sensorTruthGateRules.ts)
+ 26 tests. Runs before any LLM/vision model; after this layer no skill
consumes raw sensor rows directly (exit gate).

### Composition, not a second rule system
A 5-agent reuse-mapping pass found the existing rule surface heavily
fragmented (~14 staleness thresholds, 5 pH ranges, 10 VPD
implementations, 6 source unions). The gate therefore **imports every
threshold from its existing authority** and defines none of its own:
- **Source vocab**: `CANONICAL_SENSOR_SOURCES`
(`sensorIngestProvenance`) with deny-by-default normalization —
vendor/transport/unknown labels classify `invalid`, never `live`; only
the two sanctioned legacy aliases map (`imported`→`csv`, `sim`→`demo`,
warned).
- **Realism/suspicion**: `classifyManualMetric` + predicates from
`sensorTruthRules` (EC µS-as-mS at ≥20, stuck-RH, realism windows).
- **Freshness**: live = shared 15-min window; non-live =
`resolveStaleWindowMs` per-source registry (24h manual doctrine); future
skew = shared 5-min limit. Zero new constants.
- **Units/VPD**: `temperatureUnits`, `ecUnits.toCanonicalMscm`,
`vpdRules.calculateAirVpdKpa`.
- **F/C confusion with no new band**: a temperature failing realism in
its declared unit but plausible in the other unit is suspicious by
construction.

### Hard rules (spec + AGENTS.md)
Demo/CSV/manual never become live · missing values never become 0 (incl.
missing `vpd_kpa`) · invalid/stale never supports a healthy conclusion ·
`vpd_kpa` never derived from invalid/degraded/stale/untrusted temp or RH
(stuck-at-0 RH blocks derivation) · conflicting sensors are surfaced
(`SENSOR_CONFLICT_TOLERANCES` — a genuinely new capability, documented
as such) and never silently averaged; aggregation only under an explicit
rule over usable values only · same rows + injected `nowMs` →
byte-identical output (locked via `serializeSkillContract`).

### Interop
Explicit mappers `usabilityToSnapshotStatus` / `usabilityToDbQuality`
bridge the spec-mandated usability vocab
(`usable|degraded|stale|invalid|unknown`) to the existing
`SnapshotStatus` contract and persisted DB quality — no third competing
vocabulary left unmapped. A compile-time lock ties Build 1's
`SKILL_SENSOR_SOURCE_LABELS` to the provenance canon.

### Verification
`tsc -p tsconfig.app.json` ✅ · new suite 26/26 ✅ ·
`cross-ingest-vpd-regression`, `action-queue-safety`,
`vpd-stage-normalization-ownership` scanners ✅ · Prettier + ESLint ✅.

fix(ai-doctor): make live review history trustworthy (#324)

## Summary
- map validated live AI Doctor results into the canonical persisted
diagnosis contract used by history
- keep diagnosis visible even when persistence fails, with a calm retry
path that never invokes AI or spends a second credit
- reuse one client-generated session UUID across retries and verify
duplicate-key success only through an owner-scoped read
- freeze sensor evidence time at review submission and preserve
approval-required suggestion semantics
- invalidate AI Doctor history and timeline-memory queries after durable
saves, including after the review component unmounts
- expose allowlisted, secret-safe persistence diagnostics without
rendering raw database errors

## Safety
- no schema, migration, RLS, grant, edge-function, billing, AI-credit,
alert, Action Queue, sensor, or device-control changes
- no automatic Action Queue writes
- watch risk maps to medium and high risk maps to high; no persisted
risk understatement
- persistence failure never hides a completed diagnosis

CLEAN

TypeScript check, docs safety all passed

- `bun run test:security-static`: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed
- browser harness in installed Chrome: successful save and

build gate
- the separate production Quick Log database rollout remains blocked
because the configured Supabase connector exposes only the documented
development sandbox, not the Lovable-managed production project

Message:
Instrument privacy-safe Quick Log activation (#302)

## Summary
- complete the privacy-safe `quick_log_saved` contract across every
genuine mounted Quick Log persistence path
- keep the shared save hook telemetry-default-off so AI Doctor and
ECOWITT diary writes cannot inflate activation
- preserve semantic observation/environment categories even when legacy
persistence normalizes them to `note`
- document the GA4 client-observed activation proxy: >=3 confirmed Quick
Logs in a trailing 7-day window

## Measurement boundary
- this is a client-observed GA4 proxy, not an authoritative
server/cross-device/signup-cohort metric
- no historical backfill
- consent, blockers, connectivity, or unavailable analytics may
undercount
- event payload is a closed `event_type` only; no IDs, notes, names,
strains, sensor values, URLs, or raw payloads

## Safety and behavior
- successful canonical writes emit once
- validation failures, persistence failures, and `reused: true` replies
emit zero
- attachment-only success does not count
- AI Doctor and ECOWITT successful diary writes are explicitly proven to
emit zero
- no schema, RLS, onboarding, checkout, AI-provider, sensor-ingest,
automation, or device-control changes

## Validation
- post-latest-base focused run: 125/125 passed across 8 files
- broader implementation closure: 289/289 passed across 20 files
- typecheck: 0 errors
- diff check: clean
- independent final review: APPROVE, high confidence, no P0-P2 findings

## Deferred
Authoritative cross-device and signup-cohort activation reporting
requires a future server-side aggregate and remains intentionally out of
scope.

Author: Verdant
Message:
MCP sensor snapshot fixes + SENSOR TRUTH trust guidance — deploy mirror (#256)

Deploy-branch mirror of the PR #253 review fixes — the live MCP server
deploys from this branch, so the behavior fixes must land here as well
as on `main` (see
https://github.com/Verdant-OS/verdant-grow-diary/pull/255 for the full
write-up of all 14 findings plus the two merge-review P1s).

**This PR explicitly requests an update to the `mcp` Edge Function**
(`supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts`). The change is minimal and additive:
it only alters the `get_latest_sensor_snapshot` query strategy and the
description/instruction strings; no schema, RLS, or auth changes.

Every file shared with `main` is committed with the **exact same blobs**
as the main PR.

## What changes

- `get_latest_sensor_snapshot`: latest row per metric under
`COALESCE(captured_at, ts)` semantics — two candidates per metric
(newest captured row + newest legacy null-captured row), winner by
effective capture time with `ts`/`id` tie-breakers. A bursty metric can
no longer evict another metric's latest reading, and an old captured
bridge row can no longer beat a newer legacy manual row.
- Trust guidance per the canonical SENSOR TRUTH contract: a reading is
current live telemetry **only** when quality is `ok` AND source is
`live`; manual stays manual, csv stays csv, demo stays demo, and
`sim`/`stale`/`invalid`/unknown labels are never current or healthy.
Applied to the tool description, server instructions, presenter view,
the committed `.lovable/mcp/manifest.json`, and the Edge Function
bundle.
- Test coverage: manifest drift checks titles/descriptions; RLS fixtures
cover the wider vocabulary, the canonical trust rule, the
>50-rows-one-metric boundary, captured_at-beats-ts backfill, and the
null-captured_at coalesce regression.
- `scripts/sanitize-mcp-rls-artifacts.mjs` hardening (multiline
`raw_payload` blocks, header values, non-JWT token values) + direct unit
tests; static harness-unavailable status on the Agent Integrations page.

## First-push CI triage (all 8 failing jobs were this mirror, now fixed)

- `agent-integrations-page.test.tsx` +
`agent-integrations-a11y.test.tsx` (deploy-branch-only files): pinned
the old dead-end Verify button (`not_checked` default, button in tab
order). Updated to the new static harness-unavailable contract; all
adapter-injected verify states are unchanged and still covered.
- `mcp-manifest-drift.test.ts` + `mcp-local-rls-integration.test.ts`:
the first mirror push wrongly omitted `.lovable/mcp/manifest.json` (a
tooling artifact made it look uncommitted on this branch), so the
stricter drift assertions compared new source text against the old
committed manifest. The manifest is now updated in this PR; Lovable's
next cloud regen from `src/lib/mcp` reproduces the same content.

No pre-existing base failures were identified — every first-push failure
traced back to this mirror.

## Intentionally excluded on this branch

- `package.json` / `bun.lock` pin of `@lovable.dev/mcp-js` — Lovable
owns dependency resolution here; changing the pin without its lockfile
risks breaking the cloud build (pinned on `main`).

## Verification plan (if applying/validating via Lovable instead of
merging directly)

Follow the standard validation order — typecheck → targeted tests →
static safety → build — and keep verification in a **separate prompt**
from the build prompt (a stopped browser-test step can lose same-prompt
build work):

1. **Build prompt**: apply this change, explicitly requesting the `mcp`
Edge Function update (Lovable will not touch Edge Functions unprompted).
2. **Verification prompt**:
- Direct authed edge-function call repro: seed 50+ rows on one metric
plus an older row on another metric in a test tent →
`get_latest_sensor_snapshot` must still include the other metrics. Also
seed a newer manual row with `captured_at NULL` vs an older bridge row
with `captured_at` set → the manual row must win.
   - Re-call after the fix to confirm the full per-metric snapshot.
   - Deno edge tests pinning latest-per-metric + coalesce semantics.
- Optionally, browser-test `/settings/agent-integrations` (static
"unavailable" verify panel, updated tool description).

Message:
Fix MCP sensor snapshot truncation/ordering and stale trust vocabulary (#255)

Addresses all 14 Copilot/Codex inline review findings on #253 (the MCP
server port). Every finding also applies to the live deployed server; a
byte-identical mirror PR (#256) targets the `verdant-grow-diary` deploy
branch.

## Behavior fixes (`get_latest_sensor_snapshot`)

- **Truncation bug**: the handler ran one global `ORDER BY ts DESC LIMIT
50` and reduced to first-row-per-metric in JS, so 50+ newer rows on one
noisy metric silently evicted another metric's latest reading from the
snapshot. Now fetches the latest row **per metric** (bounded `LIMIT 1`
queries over the schema's metric allow-list), making eviction
structurally impossible.
- **Ordering semantics**: "latest" now means `COALESCE(captured_at, ts)`
— capture time when recorded, ingest time for legacy null-captured rows.
PostgREST cannot order by that expression (and `captured_at DESC NULLS
LAST` alone ranks every captured row above every legacy row regardless
of recency — caught in merge review), so each metric fetches two
candidates (newest captured row + newest legacy row by `ts`) and the
winner is picked by effective capture time with `ts`/`created_at`/`id`
tie-breakers. The true coalesce-max is provably one of the two
candidates.

## Trust vocabulary (canonical SENSOR TRUTH contract, deny-by-default)

The tool description, server instructions, `.lovable/mcp/manifest.json`,
and `manifestView.ts` all claimed sources were `manual/pi_bridge/sim`
with only `sim` non-live. Per the canonical SENSOR TRUTH contract
(Lovable knowledge pack), all four surfaces now teach the exact rule:
canonical source labels are exactly
`live/manual/csv/demo/stale/invalid`; a reading is current live
telemetry **only** when quality is `ok` AND source is `live` (fresh
validated connected telemetry); every other source or quality keeps its
label and is never live — manual stays manual, csv stays csv, demo stays
demo, and `sim`/`stale`/`invalid`/unknown labels are never current or
healthy.

## Drift protection

- `mcp-manifest-drift.test.ts` now compares **titles and descriptions**
across source tool definitions ↔ generated manifest ↔ presenter view
(previously only parameter names/required flags). The new assertions
immediately caught a second stale description
(`list_recent_diary_entries` in `manifestView.ts`), fixed here.
- `mcp-local-rls-integration.test.ts`: fixtures now cover
canonical/vendor/simulated source labels and a non-`ok` quality; a new
always-run contract test pins the canonical trust rule verbatim; new
harness-gated boundary tests seed 60 rows on one metric + an older row
on another (regression for the truncation bug) and a backfill pair where
the newest-`ts` row is not the newest capture (regression for the
ordering fix).

## Supply chain / tooling

- `@lovable.dev/mcp-js` pinned exactly at `0.20.0` — the range resolved
0.20.1 in `bun.lock` while the committed bundle imports 0.20.0, so a
cloud regen would have churned the "byte-identical" artifacts.
- `scripts/sanitize-mcp-rls-artifacts.mjs`: now also redacts non-JWT
refresh/access/bridge token values, client secrets, authorization/cookie
header values, and `raw_payload` in free text (the workflow uploads
`vitest-output.log`, and a failing leakage assertion prints the received
payload verbatim). raw_payload values are redacted as balanced multiline
blocks via a string-aware brace scan — a regex-to-end-of-line rule would
leak every line of a pretty-printed payload after the first (also caught
in merge review); truncated blocks redact to end of input.
`sanitizeText` is exported with direct unit tests
(`mcp-rls-artifact-sanitizer.test.ts`).
- `AgentIntegrations`: the production route mounts the page with
`defaultBrowserHarness` (`available: false` always), so the Verify
button's only reachable answer was "harness unavailable". It now renders
a static non-interactive unavailable status; the interactive flow
remains for injected adapters, covered by a new page-level test.

## Regression fixtures

Harness-gated RLS cases now pin: the >50-rows-one-metric boundary,
captured_at-beats-ts backfill, and the null-captured_at coalesce shape
(newer manual row with `captured_at NULL` must beat an older bridge row
with `captured_at` set).

Also adds the generated bundle to `.prettierignore` so a repo-wide
`prettier --write .` cannot reformat esbuild output into app style.

## Deployment note

`supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts` is **hand-mirrored** from the source
edits in bundle style (local regen writes a broken stub on Windows;
Lovable's cloud build is the generator of record).
Description/instruction strings were verified byte-identical across
source ↔ bundle ↔ manifest ↔ presenter view. Fixing main alone does not
change production — mirror PR #256 to `verdant-grow-diary` carries the
same blobs.

## Verification

- `vitest`: all MCP suites green (drift, manifest hash, harness ops,
schema safety, sanitizer, verify-access, new page test) plus the
`action-queue-safety` static scanner; harness-gated RLS tests run in the
`mcp-local-rls-integration` workflow.
- `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` clean; `eslint` 0 errors on
changed files; `prettier` clean.

## Summary

Brings the deployed MCP surface (**verdant-grow-os-mcp v0.1.0**) from
the `verdant-grow-diary` deploy branch onto `main`, byte-identical to
`origin/verdant-grow-diary` (audited against the live endpoint before
porting).

- **Server + tools** (`src/lib/mcp/`): server definition and 3
read-only, RLS-scoped tools — `list_grows`, `list_recent_diary_entries`,
`get_latest_sensor_snapshot`. Ownership pre-checks are included: diary
entries are gated on grow visibility (closes the operator-wide
`diary_entries` SELECT scope, per #130) and sensor snapshots are gated
on tent ownership. No service-role usage, no `raw_payload` exposure;
sensor `source`/`quality` labels preserved verbatim.
- **Generated artifacts committed exactly as deployed**:
`supabase/functions/mcp/index.ts` and `.lovable/mcp/manifest.json`. Only
Lovable's cloud build regenerates these — a local Windows build writes a
broken stub, so do not regenerate or reformat them.
- **UI**: Agent Integrations page at `/settings/agent-integrations` +
`ManifestSummaryModal` + `usePageSeo` hook.
- **Tests + CI**: all 7 MCP test files, the local RLS harness helper
(self-skips without `MCP_LOCAL_RLS_HARNESS=1` + local Supabase env),
artifact sanitizer script, and the `mcp-local-rls-integration` workflow.
- **Wiring**: `@lovable.dev/mcp-js` dependency (zod stays v3 — peer
range is `>=3.23.0`), `test:mcp:rls:local` script, `mcpPlugin()` in vite
config, route registration, and the README "Local MCP RLS integration
test" section required by the harness docs contract test.

## Test plan

- [x] `bun run typecheck` clean
- [x] All 7 MCP test files green (71 passed, 46 harness cases skip
without local stack)
- [x] Route snapshot / route manifest / auth-redirect guards green
- [x] README, architecture, and launch-readiness docs contracts green
- [x] ESLint + prettier clean on all hand-edited files
- [x] Staged MCP files verified byte-identical to
`origin/verdant-grow-diary`
- [x] PR CI green (full sharded suite + scanners) after two follow-up
commits: e0044c1b3 registered the route in the app route manifest (the
route-manifest sync guardrail, with prettier normalization of that file)
and c5bc026f5 ported the deploy branch's formatting-agnostic assertion
fix for the post-grow-reflection static-safety test.

pass would reformat the Lovable-generated `manifest.json` away from its
generator's output; the hook's checks (prettier/eslint/tsc) were run
manually on all hand-edited files instead.

Author: cheekhimself
Message:
Harden MCP local RLS harness ops: failure artifacts, manifest-driven cases, CI readiness (#131)

## Summary

Operational hardening of the local MCP RLS integration harness —
**tests/docs/CI/package script only**. No product UI, schema, RLS
policy, Edge Function, auth, or MCP tool behavior changes.

### 1. Failure-only sanitized CI artifacts

- The harness writes sanitized debug output (harness call log + response
snapshots + README.txt) under `artifacts/mcp-local-rls/`; the workflow
tees vitest output there too.
- The workflow uploads that directory **only on `if: failure()`**, after
a second sanitization pass by `scripts/sanitize-mcp-rls-artifacts.mjs`.
- The shared sanitizer (`src/test/helpers/mcpRlsHarnessOps.ts`) redacts:
JWT-like strings, bearer tokens, `sb_secret_`/`sb_publishable_` key
formats, and — by key name — access/refresh/bridge tokens, client
secrets, `service_role`, apikey/authorization/raw headers, cookies,
sessions, passwords, and `raw_payload`; live
`LOCAL_SUPABASE_*`/`SUPABASE_*` env values are stripped from all text.
- No env files, Supabase config, or key material are ever in the upload
path; `artifacts/` is gitignored.

### 2. Manifest-driven RLS isolation cases

- Pagination/filter params are **derived from
`.lovable/mcp/manifest.json`** at collection time: `limit` variants use
the advertised schema `minimum`/`maximum`, boolean filters exercise both
values, uuid scope params (`growId`/`tentId`) become the own-vs-foreign
ownership axis. Cursor/date params are recognized but never given
fabricated values — **params are never invented**.
- Every generated case runs as User A and User B, asserts rows stay
caller-scoped (id-set checks + per-user leak markers embedded in seeded
names/notes), probes foreign scope ids, re-checks unauthenticated
rejection, envelope shape, and the secret scanner.
- `get_latest_sensor_snapshot` advertises no pagination/filter params →
recorded as **N/A** by the manifest contract test and the
generated-coverage block; it still gets the baseline
ownership/unauthenticated coverage.
- Explicit `limit`/`includeArchived` regression tests are kept alongside
the generated cases.

### 3. Harness updated to the current live contract

The pre-existing harness seeded columns that no longer exist
(`diary_entries.event_type`, wide `sensor_readings` columns) and
asserted the old snapshot shape — it would have failed at seeding once
actually enabled. It now matches the schema and tools as of #130:
long-format `sensor_readings` (metric/value rows), diary seeding ordered
by `entry_at`, ownership-gated errors for foreign grow/tent ids,
per-metric snapshot shape, and the real `source`
(`manual`/`pi_bridge`/`sim`) and `quality`
(`ok`/`degraded`/`stale`/`invalid`) vocabularies.

### 4. CI readiness + migrations

- Local keys are masked with `::add-mask::` before any later step runs.
- Bounded retry loops (30×2s) verify auth + REST endpoints before and
after migrations, with clear `::error` messages and no key output.
- `supabase db reset --local` applies and verifies repo migrations
deterministically before the harness runs; `supabase migration list
--local` is echoed for the log.
- Hard lines kept and enforced by a unit test on the workflow file: no
`supabase link`, no remote `db push`, no hosted refs, no repo secrets.

### 5. Ops surface

- `package.json`: `"test:mcp:rls:local": "bunx vitest run
src/test/mcp-local-rls-integration.test.ts"` — no keys embedded
(unit-tested).
- README: documents the exact env vars, the `bun run test:mcp:rls:local`
command, CI behavior, failure-artifact sanitization guarantees, and the
never-commit-service-role-keys reminder.

## Validation (exact counts)

| Command | Result |
|---|---|
| `tsc -p tsconfig.app.json --noEmit` | clean, 0 errors |
| `vitest run src/test/mcp-local-rls-integration.test.ts` (no env) | 50
tests: **4 passed** (manifest contract), **46 skipped** (harness gated —
clean skip confirmed) |
| `vitest run src/test/mcp-rls-harness-ops.test.ts` | **20 passed**
(sanitizer, artifact writer, param derivation, script/README/workflow
contracts) |
| `vitest run` mcp-tools-schema-safety + mcp-tools-source-safety +
mcp-manifest-drift + mcp-manifest-hash | **all passed** — combined run:
6 files passed, **64 passed / 46 skipped (110 total)** |
| `node scripts/sanitize-mcp-rls-artifacts.mjs <tmp>` smoke | Bearer JWT
→ `[REDACTED]`, plain lines preserved |

Not run here: the live harness against a local Supabase (no local stack
in this environment). The CI workflow exercises it end-to-end; note its
triggers are `main`-scoped, so a `workflow_dispatch` run on this branch
is the quickest way to see it green.

## Safety

- No hosted Supabase, no production secrets, no `supabase link`, no
remote `db push`, no printed keys (masked + doubly sanitized artifacts).
- No product behavior, schema, RLS, Edge Function, auth, or MCP tool
changes.
